Detentore di animali da laboratorio (m/f/d) – specializzato in isolatori 80%-100%, Zurigo, stampa permanente Stampa Lavorare dove la ricerca plasma il futuro: al Centro di fenomica dell'ETH (EPIC) dell'ETH di Zurigo diamo un importante contributo alla moderna ricerca biomedica. Siamo specializzati nell'allevamento e nella cura degli animali da laboratorio, sempre secondo i più alti standard di qualità, igiene e benessere degli animali. Un'area centrale del nostro funzionamento degli animali sono le unità di isolamento. In questi ambienti altamente standardizzati, gli animali vengono accuditi in condizioni rigorosamente controllate e collaborano con vari gruppi di ricerca all'interno dell'ETH di Zurigo. Per rafforzare il nostro team, cerchiamo una persona impegnata ed entusiasta di questo compito specializzato e responsabile. Descrizione del lavoro

• Documentazione attenta di tutti i processi di lavoro nel sistema elettronico di gestione della stalla per animali (Vivarium)
• Manutenzione, controllo e verifica funzionale dei sistemi di isolamento e delle relative strutture tecniche

chevron ha lasciato Panoramica chevron ha lasciato Panoramica Dipendenti: in gestione speciale dei rifiuti (m/w/d) 60%-80%, Zurigo, stampa illimitata Stampa Il Dipartimento di Sicurezza, Salute e Ambiente (SGU) consiglia, sostiene e consiglia tutte le unità organizzative e membri di ETH Zurich in materia di sicurezza e salute sul lavoro, nonché sulla protezione ambientale sul lavoro. Abbiamo un'adeguata organizzazione di emergenza per l'evento. Nella vita quotidiana così come nel caso, lavoriamo a stretto contatto con le autorità e gli agenti esterni. SGU coordina l'adozione di rifiuti speciali a ETH ed è responsabile della sua eliminazione conforme. Al fine di soddisfare questi compiti in modo professionale ed efficiente, stiamo cercando una personalità esperta ed entusiasta nella sezione Sicurezza del lavoro, Salute e Ambiente. Pronto ad assumersi la responsabilità per la gestione dei rifiuti speciali conforme? Nell'ambito della sezione "Environment Team" di Sicurezza del lavoro, Salute e Ambiente Lei svolge compiti operativi e amministrativi e svolge il ruolo di un funzionario di merci pericolose nel campo della gestione speciale dei rifiuti. Si prendono rifiuti chimici liquidi e solidi nei siti di smaltimento rifiuti speciali di ETH, classificare e bere. Inoltre, è uno dei vostri compiti registrare rifiuti speciali tramite lo strumento "VeVa-Online" e creare note di accompagnamento per il trasporto. È auto-evidente informarvi attivamente sulle nuove tecnologie e materiali (ad esempio accumulatori di litio-ione, nanomateriali) e sullo sviluppo associato e discuterne nel team. Inoltre, si consiglia ai membri dell'ETH di conoscere i temi della gestione dei rifiuti speciali e delle merci pericolose e di guidarli attraverso i centri di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali, sia in tedesco che in inglese. Il vostro lavoro è la base per lo smaltimento legale e ambientale di rifiuti speciali a ETH.
• Consulenza professionale del cliente in tedesco e inglese (Niveau B2)
• Apertura per le innovazioni e ulteriori sviluppi nel campo dell'assistenza specializzata
• Partecipazione attiva e introduzione di idee proprie Offriamo la vostra professione con effetto: Fa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo supporta il vostro sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente ai cambiamenti positivi nella società. Lavorare al Vice-Presidium for Infrastructure and Sustainability (VPIN) significa plasmare attivamente il futuro dell'ETH Zurigo - un'istituzione ispiratrice, internazionale e innovativa. Il vostro impegno crea le migliori condizioni per l'eccellenza nell'insegnamento, nella ricerca, nel trasferimento di conoscenze e nella sostenibilità dell'ETH Zurigo. In un'atmosfera aperta e stimolante, fiducia, affidabilità e rispetto reciproco costituiscono la base della nostra cooperazione. Vi offriamo non solo la sicurezza, ma anche una vasta gamma di possibilità per un ulteriore sviluppo. Vi aspettiamo per lavorare in un ambiente innovativo e a valore aggiunto che si può aiutare a modellare e che apre nuove prospettive.

chevron left Overview chevron left Overview Employees:in special waste management (m/w/d) 60%-80%, Zurich, unlimited print Print The Department of Safety, Health and Environment (SGU) advises, supports and advises all organizational units and members of ETH Zurich in matters of safety and health at work as well as on environmental protection at work. We have an appropriate emergency organisation for the event. In everyday life as well as in the event, we work closely with authorities and external agents. SGU coordinates the adoption of special waste at ETH and is responsible for its compliant disposal. In order to fulfill these tasks professionally and efficiently, we are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic personality in the Work Safety, Health and Environment section. Ready to take responsibility for the compliant special waste management? As part of the "Environment Team" section of Work Safety, Health and Environment You carry out operational and administrative tasks and perform the role of a hazardous goods officer in the field of special waste management. You take liquid and solid chemical waste into the special waste disposal sites of ETH, classify and drink it. Furthermore, it is one of your tasks to register special waste via the "VeVa-Online" tool and to create accompanying notes for transport. It is self-evident to inform you actively about new technologies and materials (e.g. lithium-ion accumulators, nanomaterials) and the associated development and to discuss this in the team. In addition, you advise ETH members on the topics of special waste management and hazardous goods and guide them through the special waste disposal centres, both in German and in English. Your work is the basis for the legal and environmentally sound disposal of special waste at ETH.
• Professional consultancy of the customer in German and English (Niveau B2)
• Openness for innovations and further developments in the field of specialized care
• Active participation and introduction of own ideas We offer your profession with effect: Be part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive changes in society. Working at the Vice-Presidium for Infrastructure and Sustainability (VPIN) means actively shaping the future of ETH Zurich - an inspiring, international and innovative institution. Your commitment creates the best conditions for excellence in teaching, research, knowledge transfer and sustainability at ETH Zurich. In an open, inspiring atmosphere, trust, reliability and mutual respect form the foundation of our cooperation. We offer you not only safety, but also a wide range of possibilities for further development. We are waiting for you to work in an innovative and value-adding environment that you can help shape and which opens up new perspectives.

Mitarbeiter:in Sonderabfallentsorgung (m/w/d) 60%-80%, Zürich, unbefristet print Drucken Die Abteilung Sicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt (SGU) berät, unterstützt und schult sämtliche Organisationseinheiten und Angehörigen der ETH Zürich bei Fragen zu Sicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz am Arbeitsplatz sowie zum betrieblichem Umweltschutz. Für den Ereignisfall unterhalten wir eine angemessene Notfallorganisation. Im Alltag wie auch im Ereignisfall arbeiten wir eng mit Behörden und externen Einsatzkräften zusammen. SGU koordiniert die Annahme von Sonderabfällen an der ETH und ist für deren konforme Entsorgung verantwortlich. Um diese Aufgaben professionell und effizient erfüllen zu können, suchen wir in der Sektion Arbeitssicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt ab sofort eine erfahrene und begeisterungsfähige Persönlichkeit. Stellenbeschreibung Bereit, Verantwortung für die konforme Sonderabfallentsorgung zu übernehmen? Als Teil des «Umwelt-Teams» der Sektion Arbeitssicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt übernimmst Du operative und administrative Aufgaben und nimmst die Rolle eines Gefahrgutbeauftragten im Bereich Sonderabfallentsorgung wahr. Du nimmst flüssige und feste Chemikalienabfälle in den Sonderabfallentsorgungsstellen der ETH an, klassierst und triagierst diese. Desweiteren gehört es zu deinen Aufgaben, Sonderabfälle über das Tool «VeVa-Online» anzumelden und Begleitscheine für den Transport zu erstellen. Es ist für Dich selbstverständlich, Dich aktiv über neue Technologien und Materialien (z.B. Lithium-Ionen-Akkumulatoren, Nanomaterialien) und die damit einhergehende Entwicklung zu infomieren und dies im Team zu diskutieren. Darüber hinaus berätst Du ETH-Angehörige zu den Themen Sonderabfallentsorgung und Gefahrgut und machst Führungen durch die Sonderabfallentsorgungsstellen, sowohl auf Deutsch als auch auf Englisch. Deine Arbeit ist die Grundlage für die gesetzeskonforme und umweltverträgliche Entsorgung von Sonderabfällen an der ETH. Profil
• Abgeschlossene naturwissenschaftliche oder technische Ausbildung
• Fundierte Kenntnisse für die sichere Annahme von Sonderabfällen

Zürich, Basel, Schlieren) Arbeitsort Arbeitsort Wir bieten Dein Beruf mit Wirkung: Werde Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur deine berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt. Dein Engagement schafft beste Voraussetzungen für Exzellenz in Lehre, Forschung, Wissenstransfer und Nachhaltigkeit der ETH Zürich. In einer offenen, inspirierenden Atmosphäre bilden Vertrauen, Verlässlichkeit und gegenseitiger Respekt das Fundament unserer Zusammenarbeit. Wir bieten dir nicht nur Sicherheit, sondern auch vielfältige Weiterentwicklungsmöglichkeiten. Descrizione Ricerca post-dottorale in termini di genomica e diversità transposonale comparata 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il nuovo gruppo Plant Disease Dynamics dell'ETH di Zurigo sta cercando di reclutare un biologo fungo del genoma interessato ai modi in cui i transposoni modellano la struttura e la funzione dei genoma patogeni vegetali. Stiamo cercando qualcuno con esperienza precedente sia in genomica comparativa fungina o transposon, che può esplorare la diversità e l'evoluzione dei transposons di Starship e dei geni e transposizioni che portano all'interno di specie fungine infettanti vegetali. Questa posizione costituisce un pilastro di un progetto di ricerca a tre pilastri, dove sarete associati con altri esperti in biochimica e biologia cellulare. L'obiettivo è quello di costruire un team interdisciplinare collaborativo che utilizza la genomica della popolazione per sostenere lo sviluppo di un'implementazione di modelli di transposon sperimentali di lavoro in laboratorio. Sfondo del progetto Il trasferimento genico orizzontale (HGT) consente la diffusione di geni patogeni tra i microbi e può quindi guidare l'emergenza di nuove malattie. Nei funghi patogeni, una minaccia globale emergente sia per gli esseri umani che per i nostri raccolti, i meccanismi che facilitano la HGT rimangono sconosciuti. Recenti lavori hanno scoperto un nuovo gruppo di transponti giganti chiamati Starships, che hanno mosso virulence, la tolleranza dei metalli e altri geni associati al fitness orizzontalmente tra le specie fungine. Questa posizione post-doctoral è focalizzata sui funghi patogeni vegetali, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum e Pyrenophora tritici-repentis che portano tutti il gene fungine di virulenza ToxA , che è annidato all'interno di un transposon passeggeri più piccolo chiamato ToxTA. Questo transposon è stato catturato indipendentemente da due diversi trasposizioni di Starship, Sanctuary e Horizon con la prova di altre catture in altre specie fungine. Cerchiamo di comprendere la storia evolutiva e il trasferimento orizzontale del transposon ToxTA nelle popolazioni naturali di tutte le specie fungine in cui si trova. Questo include oltre 300 genoma pubblicamente accessibili, così come diverse dozzine di assemblee di lunga data della collezione interna del laboratorio. Questa posizione mira a sintetizzare tutte le informazioni disponibili da questi isolati fungini naturali per costruire ipotesi per le quali le caratteristiche genetiche sono essenziali per il trasferimento orizzontale. Post-Doctoral Research in Comparative Fungal Genomics and Transposon Diversity 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The newly established Plant Disease Dynamics group at the ETH Zurich is looking to recruit a fungal genome biologist interested in the ways in which transposons shape the structure and function of plant pathogen genomes. We are looking for someone with prior experience in either fungal or transposon comparative genomics, who can explore the diversity and evolution of Starship transposons and the genes and transposons they carry within plant infecting fungal species. This position forms one pillar of a three-pillared research project, where you will be partnered with other experts in biochemistry and cell biology. The goal is to build a collaborative interdisciplinary team that uses population genomics to support the development an implementation of working experimental transposon models in the lab. Project background Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) enables the spread of pathogenicity genes between microbes and can therefore drive the emergence of novel diseases . In pathogenic fungi, an emerging global threat to both humans and our crops, the mechanisms that facilitate HGT remain unknown. Recent work has uncovered a novel group of giant transposons called Starships, which have moved virulence, metal tolerance and other fitness associated genes horizontally between fungal species. This post-doctoral positions is focused on the plant pathogenic fungi, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum and Pyrenophora tritici-repentis that all carry the fungal virulence gene ToxA , which is nested inside a smaller passenger transposon called ToxTA. This transposon has been captured independently by two different Starship transposons, Sanctuary and Horizon with evidence of other captures in other fungal species. We seek to understand the evolutionary history and horizontal transfer of the ToxTA transposon in natural populations of all fungal species in which it is found. This includes over 300 publicly accessible genomes as well as several dozen long-read assemblies from the lab's internal collection. This position aims to synthesise all available information from these natural fungal isolates to build hypotheses for which genetic features are essential for horizontal transfer. Job description
• Generate new long-read Nanopore assemblies from the labs long-term culture collection
• Assemble, annotate and quality assess all existing 30+ long-read genome assemblies
• Mine availalbe public genomes for TEs of interest
• Establish reproducible Snakemake/Nextflow pipelines to support the labs long-term research interests
• Proactively manage the labs genomic data resources
• Supervise and mentor PhD and Masters students in comparative fungal genomics
• Assist in the delivery of lectures or seminars for the Plant Disease Dynamics group
• Write and publish peer-reviewed manuscripts
• Apply for funding to develop research independence The initial contract duration is two years, with the possibility of extension. Profile

• Evidence of research excellence through peer-reviewed publications

Beschreibung Post-Doctoral Research in Comparative Fungal Genomics and Transposon Diversity 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die neu gegründete Plant Disease Dynamics-Gruppe an der ETH Zürich sucht einen Pilz-Genom-Biologe zu rekrutieren, der an der Art interessiert ist, wie Transposons die Struktur und Funktion von Pflanzenpathogen-Genomen prägen. Wir suchen jemanden mit vorheriger Erfahrung in entweder Pilz- oder Transposon vergleichende Genomik, die die Vielfalt und Evolution von Sternenschiff-Transposons und die Gene und Transposons, die sie in Pflanzen infizieren Pilzarten zu erforschen. Diese Position bildet eine Säule eines dreifachen Forschungsprojekts, in dem Sie mit anderen Experten in der Biochemie und Zellbiologie zusammenarbeiten werden. Ziel ist es, ein kollaboratives interdisziplinäres Team aufzubauen, das die Bevölkerungsgenomik nutzt, um die Entwicklung einer Implementierung von funktionierenden experimentellen Transposonmodellen im Labor zu unterstützen. Projekt Hintergrund Der horizontale Gentransfer (HGT) ermöglicht die Ausbreitung von Pathogenitätsgenen zwischen Mikroben und kann daher das Auftreten neuer Krankheiten antreiben. Bei pathogenen Pilzen, einer aufstrebenden globalen Bedrohung sowohl für Menschen als auch für unsere Kulturen, bleiben die Mechanismen, die HGT erleichtern, unbekannt. Neuere Arbeiten haben eine neue Gruppe von riesigen Transposons namens Starships entdeckt, die Virulenz, Metalltoleranz und andere Fitness-assoziierte Gene horizontal zwischen Pilzarten bewegt haben. Diese Post-Doctoral-Positionen konzentriert sich auf die pflanzenpathogenen Pilze, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum und Pyrenophora tritici-repentis, die alle die Pilzvirulenz Gen ToxA tragen, die in einem kleineren Passagier-Transposon namens ToxTA geschachtelt ist. Dieses Transposon wurde unabhängig von zwei verschiedenen Sternenschiff-Transposons, Sanctuary und Horizon mit Beweisen für andere Fänge in anderen Pilzarten gefangen genommen. Wir versuchen, die Evolutionsgeschichte und die horizontale Übertragung des ToxTA-Transposons in natürlichen Populationen aller Pilzarten zu verstehen, in denen es gefunden wird. Dazu gehören über 300 öffentlich zugängliche Genome sowie mehrere Dutzend langwierige Baugruppen aus der internen Sammlung des Labors. Diese Position zielt darauf ab, alle verfügbaren Informationen aus diesen natürlichen Pilzisolaten zu synthetisieren, um Hypothesen zu erstellen, für die genetische Merkmale für die horizontale Übertragung unerlässlich sind. Descrizione Recherche postdoctorale en génomique fongique comparée et diversité transposonienne 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le nouveau groupe Plant Disease Dynamics de l'ETH Zurich cherche à recruter un biologiste du génome fongique intéressé par la façon dont les transposons façonnent la structure et la fonction des génomes phytopathogènes. Nous recherchons une personne ayant une expérience antérieure en génomique comparée fongique ou transposon, qui peut explorer la diversité et l'évolution des transposons de vaisseau et les gènes et transposons qu'ils transportent au sein des espèces fongiques infectant les plantes. Cette position constitue un pilier d'un projet de recherche à trois piliers, où vous serez en partenariat avec d'autres experts en biochimie et en biologie cellulaire. L'objectif est de constituer une équipe interdisciplinaire collaborative qui utilise la génomique des populations pour appuyer l'élaboration d'une mise en oeuvre de modèles expérimentaux de transposition en laboratoire. Contexte du projet Le transfert horizontal de gènes (HGT) permet la propagation de gènes de pathogénicité entre microbes et peut donc conduire à l'émergence de nouvelles maladies. Chez les champignons pathogènes, une menace mondiale émergente pour les humains et nos cultures, les mécanismes qui facilitent l'HGT demeurent inconnus. Des travaux récents ont révélé un nouveau groupe de transposons géants appelés Starships, qui ont déplacé horizontalement la virulence, la tolérance aux métaux et d'autres gènes associés à la condition physique entre les espèces fongiques. Ces positions postdoctorales sont axées sur les champignons phytopathogènes, Bipolaris sorokiniana, Parastagonospora nodorum et Pyrenophora tritici-repentis qui portent tous le gène de virulence fongique ToxA , qui est niché à l'intérieur d'un petit transposon passager appelé ToxTA. Ce transposon a été capturé indépendamment par deux transposons différents de vaisseau, Sanctuaire et Horizon avec des preuves d'autres captures chez d'autres espèces fongiques. Nous cherchons à comprendre l'histoire évolutive et le transfert horizontal du ToxTA transposon dans les populations naturelles de toutes les espèces fongiques dans lesquelles il se trouve. Cela comprend plus de 300 génomes accessibles au public ainsi que plusieurs douzaines d'assemblages à lecture longue de la collection interne du laboratoire. Cette position vise à synthétiser toutes les informations disponibles de ces isolats fongiques naturels afin de construire des hypothèses pour lesquelles les caractéristiques génétiques sont essentielles au transfert horizontal. La frustrazione geometrica nei sistemi quantistici porta ad una stretta concorrenza tra stati di rotazione collettivi qualitativamente nuovi, come strutture topologiche, liquidi di rotazione quantistica, fasi ordinate multipolari e spin-supersolidi, per citarne solo alcuni. Ogni stato è caratterizzato da un proprio insieme di eccitazioni elementari che spesso non hanno un analogo nella fisica semiclassica. Il vincitore di questa competizione è di solito determinato da meccanismi noti come ordine termico e quantico-da-disordine. descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD Position: Order-from-Disorder in Frustrated Quantum Magnets 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Neutron Scattering and Magnetism Group, Physics Department, ETH Zurich, is currently looking to fill a PhD position on experimental studies of frustrated quantum magnets using neutron scattering, μSR and other techniques. Geometric frustration in quantum systems leads to a tight competition between qualitatively new collective spin states, such as topological structures, quantum spin liquids, multipolar ordered phases and spin-supersolids, to name only a few. Each state is characterized by its own set of elementary excitations that often have no analogue in semi-classical physics. The winner of this competition is usually determined by mechanisms known as thermal and quantum order-from-disorder. Controlling these offers a way to manipulate and study such exotic systems. The successful candidate will realize this control experimentally in carefully selected prototypical magnetic materials. Job description
• The work will involve synthesis and growth of single crystal samples, as well as their characterization with X-ray diffraction
• The samples will be further characteried with optical spectroscopy experiments, as well as magnetothermodynamic, magnetomechanical and magnetoacoustic measurements at mK-temperatures and high magnetic fields, using equipment available in our laboratory
• The research will culminate in neutron scattering, ultra-high-field, and muon spin rotation studies at state of the art large-scale user facilities in Switzerland, France, Germany, UK, Japan and the USA
• Data analysis and modeling will be done in collaboration with research groups that specialize in theoretical and numerical calculations Profile
• The successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in every phase of the project and to take the lead whenever possible
• No prior experience in neutron scattering is required, but a solid background in laboratory work and analysis of experimental data is a must
• Since the project is based around rather complex concepts in modern physics, a solid theoretical background in quantum mechanics, statistical physics and quantum solid state physics is absolutely essential
• Good computer skills are a plus Workplace Workplace We offer

Il Direttore Tecnico è il direttore tecnico senior di ECAF e garantisce un funzionamento sicuro, affidabile ed efficiente degli strumenti ECAF e delle strutture per gli utenti a supporto della ricerca e della formazione. descriptionByLocale.en:
Technical Director, Environmental Chemical Analysis Facility (ECAF) 80%-100%, Zurich, permanent print Drucken The Department of Environmental Systems Science (D-USYS) at ETH Zurich is seeking a Technical Director to lead the operation of the Environmental Chemical Analysis Facility (ECAF), a newly established departmental platform. The Technical Director is the senior technical manager of ECAF and ensures safe, reliable, and efficient operation of ECAF instruments and user facilities in support of research and training. This role combines operational leadership of a modern analytical facility with close scientific interaction with a diverse user community. Project background The Environmental Chemical Analysis Facility (ECAF) is a user facility for chemical analysis instrumentation supporting research and teaching across D-USYS and other ETH Zurich and ETH Domain units. The facility that includes various mass spectrometry (MS) instruments (HR-MS, ICP-MS), standalone and MS-coupled chromatography systems (GC, LC, IC), further instrumentation for elemental analyses, and instrumentation for stable isotope measurements. ECAF is being established as a robust, user-focused platform with standardized workflows, strong safety culture, and high-quality training to support chemical analyses critical for environmental research. Job description
• Facility launch: As its first Technical Director, your vision and leadership will be critical in establishing ECAF as a modern, well-run, state-of-the-art, user-focused chemical analysis facility, helping to develop its policies, procedures, user culture, and strategy.
• Facility operations: Oversee the day-to-day activities in ECAF, ensuring that instruments and user facilities are running and available.
• Scientific and research support: Support users in developing and optimizing analytical protocols for challenging analytes and complex matrices, including sample preparation workflows and QA/QC concepts. Provide consultation during experimental design (e.g., selection of analytical approach, measurement strategy, controls, and interpretation limits) and help translate research needs into analytical workflows. Where appropriate, contribute as a scientific and technical partner to research projects that rely on ECAF infrastructure.
• Supervision: Share supervision responsibilities with the ECAF faculty Director, overseeing and coordinating technical staff and student assistants.
• Maintenance and service coordination: Plan and coordinate preventive maintenance, servicing, repairs, vendor support, and service contracts.
• User access and training framework: Develop and maintain workflows for user registration, onboarding, authorization, training records, and operational oversight.
• Resource and cost oversight: Maintain the inventory and operational documentation; manage internal billing processes; provide input and guidance for annual fee setting and budget planning.

Directeur technique, Centre d ' analyse des produits chimiques en matière d ' environnement 80%-100%, Zurich, permanente imprimer Drucken Le Département des sciences des systèmes environnementaux (D-USYS) de l'ETH Zurich cherche un directeur technique pour diriger le fonctionnement de l'Environmental Chemical Analysis Facility (ECAF), une nouvelle plateforme départementale. Le directeur technique est le directeur technique principal de l'ECAF et assure la sécurité, la fiabilité et l'efficacité de l'utilisation des instruments et des installations de l'ECAF à l'appui de la recherche et de la formation. Ce rôle combine le leadership opérationnel d'une installation analytique moderne avec une interaction scientifique étroite avec une communauté d'utilisateurs diversifiée. Contexte du projet L'Environmental Chemical Analysis Facility (ECAF) est une installation d'utilisation d'instruments d'analyse chimique qui soutient la recherche et l'enseignement dans l'ensemble de D-USYS et d'autres unités du domaine de Zurich et de l'ETH. L'installation qui comprend divers instruments de spectrométrie de masse (HR-MS, ICP-MS), des systèmes de chromatographie autonomes et couplés MS (GC, LC, IC), d'autres instruments d'analyse élémentaire et des instruments de mesure des isotopes stables. L'ECAF est une plate-forme robuste axée sur les utilisateurs, dotée de flux de travail normalisés, d'une solide culture de sécurité et d'une formation de haute qualité pour appuyer les analyses chimiques essentielles à la recherche environnementale. Description du poste
• Lancement de l'installation : En tant que premier directeur technique, votre vision et votre leadership seront essentiels pour faire de l'ECAF une installation d'analyse chimique moderne, bien gérée, à la fine pointe de la technologie et axée sur les utilisateurs, contribuant ainsi à l'élaboration de ses politiques, procédures, culture des utilisateurs et stratégie.
• Exploitation des installations: Surveiller les activités quotidiennes de l'ECAF, en veillant à ce que les instruments et les installations des utilisateurs soient opérationnels et disponibles.
• Soutien scientifique et de recherche : Aider les utilisateurs à élaborer et optimiser des protocoles analytiques pour les analytes difficiles et les matrices complexes, y compris des flux de travail de préparation d'échantillons et des concepts d'AQ/CQ. Fournir des consultations pendant la conception expérimentale (p. ex., choix de l'approche analytique, stratégie de mesure, contrôles et limites d'interprétation) et aider à traduire les besoins de recherche en flux de travail analytiques. Le cas échéant, contribuer en tant que partenaire scientifique et technique à des projets de recherche reposant sur l'infrastructure de l'ECAF.
• Supervision: partager les responsabilités de supervision avec le directeur du corps professoral de l'ECAF, superviser et coordonner le personnel technique et les assistants étudiants.
• Coordination de l'entretien et des services : planifier et coordonner l'entretien préventif, l'entretien, les réparations, l'appui aux fournisseurs et les contrats de services.
• Cadre d'accès et de formation des utilisateurs: Élaborer et maintenir des flux de travail pour l'enregistrement des utilisateurs, l'embarquement, l'autorisation, les dossiers de formation et la supervision opérationnelle.
• Contrôle des ressources et des coûts : tenir à jour l'inventaire et la documentation opérationnelle; gérer les processus de facturation interne; fournir des intrants et des conseils pour l'établissement annuel des frais et la planification budgétaire.
• Gouvernance et coordination des parties prenantes: devenir membre de la direction du CAF et contribuer à la planification opérationnelle, à la mise en œuvre des politiques et à l'amélioration continue des processus d'installation. Profil
• Formation : Diplôme de maîtrise en chimie analytique, sciences de l'environnement ou domaine connexe, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
• Expertise technique: expérience démontrée avec des instruments analytiques modernes et des flux de travail en laboratoire (par exemple, LC-MS, GC, PIC, IC, analyse élémentaire, spectroscopie optique ou plateformes comparables).
• Leadership opérationnel : Capacité de gérer une infrastructure de laboratoire complexe, de coordonner les fournisseurs et les fournisseurs de services et de maintenir des systèmes de documentation robustes.
• Compétences en matière de personnes et de communication : forte orientation des services et compétences en matière de communication; capacité de travailler avec divers groupes d'utilisateurs et équilibrer les priorités concurrentes.

Il nostro gruppo indaga le interazioni degli insetti vegetali utilizzando approcci comportamentali, chimici e molecolari. Siamo alla ricerca di uno studente motivato per sostenere un progetto di ricerca sulle risposte di fioritura in diverse specie vegetali a seguito di danni a foglia inflitti da bumblebee. Il progetto prevede sia la manutenzione degli impianti che il lavoro sperimentale con bumblebees, compresi i trattamenti di bee-damage. Il ruolo è adatto a uno studente affidabile e organizzato che gode di lavoro pratico con piante, insetti e esperimenti a effetto serra. PhD position: Structure-activity relationships for CO2 capture materials 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (LESE, ETH Zürich) invites applications for a PhD position in the field of CO2 capture, with a focus on structure–performance relationships. At LESE, our research aims to obtain a fundamental understanding of materials that allow for the capture and/or conversion of CO2. This PhD position is funded by the National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Separations. Job description
• Within a broader research program that integrates process modelling, computational materials screening and discovery, experimental synthesis, and mechanistic and performance assessment under application-relevant conditions for separation technologies, this project aims to accelerate the identification of novel materials for CO2 capture
• Specifically, this PhD project combines the synthesis of model materials as well as their operando characterization and molecular modelling to identify new CO2 sorbent families and to establish structure–performance relationships
• Concerning the experimental techniques employed, this PhD position will focus on (operando) X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray total scattering, and vibrational spectroscopies Profile
• Applicants for this PhD position are expected to have an excellent MSc degree in Chemical Engineering, Material Science, or Chemistry
• Experience and knowledge in material synthesis and/or (structural) material characterization are highly valued
• We are looking for highly motivated, committed, and creative individuals who can work in a team and have outstanding communication skills
• Working in a top-level research environment with advanced laboratory infrastructure, the candidate will have a unique opportunity to develop their research abilities

Chez LESE, notre recherche vise à obtenir une compréhension fondamentale des matériaux qui permettent la capture et/ou la conversion du CO2. Group Leader Clinical Bioinformatics 80%-100%, Basel, permanent print Drucken The ETH Zurich technology platform NEXUS Personalized Health enables discovery and translational research for personalized health. We offer a broad range of expertise across Clinical Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Software Engineering, Systems Operations, and Screening & Lab Automation. Embedded in this multi-disciplinary environment, the Clinical Bioinformatics group translates computational biology into clinically usable outcomes, working deliberately across the boundary between biomedical research and clinical practice. Our work includes project-tailored analyses and integration of high-dimensional molecular data, spanning from whole-genome variant calling and decision support to single-cell sequencing analysis. We develop and extend robust analysis workflows and reusable components, in close collaboration with academic institutions and hospitals. Job description As Group Leader Clinical Bioinformatics, you lead a team of bioinformatics analysts and software engineers. You ensure that analyses and workflows are reproducible, scalable, and fit for translational and clinical contexts. You drive innovation by continuously evaluating emerging technologies and analytical approaches, integrating cutting-edge methods into clinical and translational research. A key part of the role is securing, prioritizing, and strategically managing clinical and translational projects through active stakeholder engagement.
• Project management: structure and oversee projects end-to-end, ensuring clear scope definition, milestone planning, risk management, documentation standards, and processes aligned with translational and clinical quality requirements
• Technical leadership: drive development and extension of pipelines using Nextflow and Snakemake. Set standards for workflow engineering, testing, documentation, and long-term maintainability
• Delivery ownership: take responsibility for timelines, quality, and stakeholder alignment across multiple projects with variable scope
• Project acquisition and customer management: build relationships with researchers, clinicians, and partners, shape projects, and translate needs into clear deliverables and expectations
• Clinical reporting and decision support: turn complex, multimodal, and large-scale results into clear outputs for physicians, including dashboards and web-based reporting for decision support
• Clinician partnership: listen closely, clarify what is useful, and keep the interface simple while your team handles technical complexity
• Innovation and scientific advancement: stay at the forefront of developments in bioinformatics, AI, and data-driven medicine, evaluate emerging methods and technologies, and translate promising approaches into robust, clinically applicable solutions
• Cross-team collaboration: work closely with the Software Engineering, Systems Operations, Biostatistics, and Screening & Lab Automation groups to deliver integrated solutions end-to-end
• People leadership: recruit, mentor, and develop team members, fostering knowledge exchange and high standards
• Resource management: plan capacity, prioritize work, and contribute to budgeting and reporting for the group Quick Self-Check You will thrive in this role if...
• You enjoy owning projects end-to-end, from shaping the initial question with clinicians and partners to delivering robust, reusable solutions with clear outcomes
• You like working across disciplines and building close collaborations with clinicians and cross-functional partners, not working in a silo
• You are comfortable setting direction, making prioritisation calls, and being accountable for timelines and quality
• You like building workflows others rely on and continuously improving them to raise reproducibility, scalability, and impact
• You can turn complex, multimodal data into decision-support outputs that are clear, usable, and focused on what physic

Postdoctoral researcher in nano-optomechanics 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We are seeking for a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our team to work at the interface between nano-optics and optomechanics. Recent advances in integrated optics and meta-optics have enabled unprecedented control over light-matter interactions, catalyzing breakthroughs in imaging, nonlinear optics, and photonic computing. We leverage these developments to advance the field of optomechanics. By exploring the interplay between optical and mechanical degrees of freedom, our group aims to unlock new frontiers in fundamental physics and quantum technologies. As a postdoctoral researcher you will integrate a dedicated team of PhD students to harness the nano- and micro-photonics toolbox for enhanced control over optomechanical interactions. Your research will be central to investigating these effects, advancing our fundamental understanding, and translating new physical phenomena into functional technologies. Job description Your work will cover all the steps from idealization of the system to its full characterization:
• Design of optomechanical systems using multiphysics numerical simulations
• Nanofabrication in state-of-the-art cleanroom environment
• Experimental characterization of their optomechanical properties While you are expected to lead your own project, you will also have the opportunity to collaborate with PhD students. Profile
• The successful candidate holds a PhD in Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, supported by a strong background in experimental laboratory work and advanced data analysis
• Experience in optomechanics, nanofabrication, nanophotonics or integrated optics, experiment control, or data analysis are beneficial
• We are looking for an individual who shares our passion for cutting-edge research, brings a high degree of motivation and creativity, and communicates with clarity
• They should enjoy working collaboratively and respectfully within a diverse team Workplace Workplace We offer The Nanophotonic Systems Laboratory provides a stimulating environment at the forefront of light-matter interaction research. We offer:
• Premier facilities: Access to world-class nanofabrication cleanrooms and advanced optical characterization labs
• Proven excellence: Integration into a group with a deep-rooted history of cutting edge research in nanophotonics and optomechanics
• Collaborative spirit: A diverse and respectful international team culture
• Professional development: Mentorship and resources to help you establish an independent scientific profile chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. L'Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) è una grande arteria del trasporto termico globale che colpisce il clima europeo e globale, che ha sostanzialmente indebolito decine di volte negli ultimi centinaia dimila anni e poi recuperato tra secoli e millenni. Questa posizione di dottorato contribuisce alla nostra continua ricerca per diagnosticare le cause di questi bruschi indebolimenti e i fattori che hanno permesso ad AMOC di recuperare. Il progetto sta generando nuovi record geochimici di stalagmiti che sono cresciuti in grotte costiere, per ricostruire la fase dei cambiamenti nella salinità dell'Atlantico settentrionale rispetto alle variazioni di AMOC, e interpretarli con l'aiuto di modelli di processo e esperimenti con tracciatori in esperimenti di circolazione generale atmosferici-ocei. PhD position: Examining the thresholds in past Atlantic Ocean circulation using stalagmite geochemistry 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken If you are intrigued by study of past climate, enjoy having your hands on samples in the lab and generating new geochemical data, and are a quantitative thinker, you might be interested in this PhD project. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major artery of global heat transport affecting European and global climate, which has substantially weakened dozens of times in the last several hundred thousand years and then recovered within centuries to millennial. This PhD position contributes to our ongoing research to diagnose the causes for these abrupt weakenings and the factors which allowed AMOC to recover. The project is generating new geochemical records from stalagmites which grew in coastal caves, to reconstruct the phasing of changes in the North Atlantic salinity relative to AMOC variations, and interpreting them with the aid of process models and experiments with tracers in atmosphere-ocean general circulation experiments. Job description
• As a PhD student, you will plan, generate, and interpret new research data; you will present data to scientific colleagues in workshops and conferences, and you will prepare your research findings for publication in scientific journals
• You will collaborate with a research team at ETH and at other institutions

• You have completed a Master's Degree relevant to Paleoclimate study (e.g Earth Science, or Atmosphere and Climate study in Physics or Geography realm)

La posizione è parte di un progetto di ricerca finanziato da SNSF che esamina come le tecnologie AI avanzate rimodellano strategia-making, progettazione organizzativa e adattamento continuo nelle organizzazioni. La Cattedra di Gestione Strategica e Innovazione offre un ambiente di ricerca ispiratore e basato su team con un gruppo dinamico e internazionale di ricercatori. SMI si impegna a ricercare al più alto livello accademico nella gestione e nel business, e il team ha un forte track record di pubblicazione in importanti riviste come Academy of Management Journal, Management Science, Organization Science, Strategic Management Journal, Academy of Management Annals e Journal of Management Studies. Questa è una posizione di dottorato nella ricerca di gestione e organizzazione, non un ruolo tecnico AI-sviluppo. Il candidato di successo studierà l'IA come un fenomeno organizzativo e strategico, con una forte attenzione alla ricerca basata sulla teoria, orientata alla pubblicazione. Il lavoro empirico coinvolgerà la ricerca sul campo in collaborazione con i principali partner aziendali, tra cui l'impegno regolare con attori e processi organizzativi. La posizione è particolarmente adatta per i candidati considerando una futura carriera in accademia. I candidati che perseguono altri percorsi a lungo termine sono benvenuti se sono fortemente motivati a sviluppare una ricerca rigorosa e mirano a pubblicare nelle principali riviste scientifiche. I candidati al dottorato sono tenuti a produrre una dissertazione di almeno tre documenti di alta qualità mirati a riviste di alto livello, con l'obiettivo di promuovere la gestione e la ricerca di organizzazione. La posizione offre una stretta supervisione, nonché l’accesso all’infrastruttura di ricerca dell’ETH di Zurigo, alla sedia SMI e all’ambiente di ricerca AI più ampio all’ETH. descriptionByLocale.it:
Dottorato in gestione forestale Effetti sulla qualità dell'acqua 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Lo studente sarà ospitato tra i gruppi WaldLab Ecohydrology e Silviculture . Il gruppo WaldLab Ecohydrology fa parte della Cattedra di Idrologia e Scienza del Sistema River presso l'Istituto ETH di Ingegneria Ambientale di Zurigo, con competenze nelle valutazioni della chimica dell'acqua negli ecosistemi forestali. Il gruppo Silviculture fa parte della Cattedra di Gestione delle Risorse Forestali presso l'Istituto ETH di Ecosistemi Terrestrial di Zurigo, con esperienza nella silvicoltura e nella gestione forestale. Stiamo cercando uno studente medico affidabile, entusiasta e altamente motivato con la passione per la scienza interdisciplinare per unirsi al nostro team. Sfondo del progetto Questa posizione fa parte del progetto “Forest Management and Drinking Water Security in Climate Change” sostenuto dall’Ufficio federale dell’ambiente. Il progetto indaga il legame critico tra la gestione degli ecosistemi forestali e la salute e la qualità dell'acqua potabile in tutta la Svizzera. Poiché il cambiamento climatico intensifica le perturbazioni come siccità, vento e focolai di parassiti, capire come la struttura forestale e la gestione influenzano i risultati della qualità dell'acqua è vitale. Attraverso la scala nazionale e i siti sperimentali, il progetto integra l'analisi dei dati a livello nazionale, il monitoraggio della qualità dell'acqua delle reti primaverili e approfondimenti meccanicistici nei tempi di instradamento e di transito dei flussi subsuperficiali. Il progetto è strettamente allineato con le parti interessate della foresta e dell'acqua potabile e le autorità decisionali; quindi, una solida e fondamentale comprensione degli ecosistemi forestali dell'Europa centrale e svizzera (compresa la composizione delle specie, le fasi di sviluppo e le pratiche silvicolturali) è essenziale per questo ruolo. Il progetto sarà realizzato in un ambiente collaborativo tra i due gruppi di ricerca, fornendo un ampio supporto tecnico e competenze interdisciplinari in ecologia e gestione forestale. Descrizione del lavoro Il progetto di dottorato si concentra sulla valutazione della resilienza delle risorse acqua potabile svizzere ai cambiamenti forestali e agli interventi di gestione. Come candidato di successo, il vostro lavoro includerà:
• Integrazione dati a livello nazionale: analisi dei gradienti nella copertura forestale e della struttura (ad esempio, miscele di specie arboree, densità) in relazione ai parametri dell'acqua potabile a lungo termine, contabilizzazione della storia dell'idrogeologia e dell'uso del suolo
• Monitoraggio del campo & Sampling: Condurre valutazioni della qualità dell'acqua in tutte le reti a molla svizzere per identificare come le pratiche di gestione influenzano la resilienza durante i disturbi causati dagli eventi
• Investigazioni Meccaniche: Monitoraggio di siti sperimentali intensivamente strumentali per determinare come la salute e la struttura della foresta alterano il flusso di subsuperficie e gli impulsi di contaminazione
• Sviluppo della sintesi e della strategia: sviluppo e valutazione di strategie di gestione adeguate per ridurre i rischi di acqua potabile
• Stakeholder Communication: Eseguire analisi statistiche e modellare per tradurre i risultati in raccomandazioni di gestione attuabili per astrazioni acquatiche La posizione a tempo pieno è finanziata per quattro anni. Le prestazioni sociali e salariali sono fornite secondo le norme dell'ETH di Zurigo. Profilo All'inizio, devi aver completato un Master in idrologia, scienze ambientali, scienze forestali, ecologia, o un campo strettamente correlato con esperienza nella chimica dell'acqua, nella silvicoltura, nel lavoro sul campo sperimentale e nell'analisi dei dati su larga scala. È necessario avere buone capacità statistiche e esperienza di programmazione (ad esempio, in R o Python). L'inglese scritto e parlato eccellente, così come la licenza del conducente, sono obbligatori. Per questo progetto, consideriamo il tedesco e altre lingue nazionali svizzere un bene. Sono previste buone capacità di scrittura e la capacità di lavorare in un ambiente interdisciplinare. Luogo di lavoro Luogo di lavoro Offriamo

Doctoral Student in Forest Management Effects on Water Quality 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The student will be hosted between the groups WaldLab Ecohydrology and Silviculture . The WaldLab Ecohydrology group is part of the Chair of Hydrology and River System Science at the ETH Zurich Institute of Environmental Engineering, with expertise in water chemistry assessments in forested ecosystems. The Silviculture group is part of the Chair of Forest Resources Management at the ETH Zurich Institute of Terrestrial Ecosystems, with expertise in silviculture and forest management. We are looking for a reliable, enthusiastic, and highly motivated doctoral student with a passion for interdisciplinary science to join our team. Project background This position is part of the project “Forest Management and Drinking Water Security under Climate Change” supported by the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment. The project investigates the critical link between forest ecosystem management and health and the quality of drinking water across Switzerland. As climate change intensifies disturbances like droughts, windthrows, and pest outbreaks, understanding how forest structure and management influence water quality outcomes is vital. Across national scale and experimental sites, the project integrates country-wide data analysis, water quality monitoring of spring networks and detailed mechanistic insights into subsurface flow routing and transit times. The project is closely aligned with forest and drinking water stakeholders and decision-making authorities; thus, a solid, fundamental understanding of Central European and Swiss forest ecosystems (including species composition, development stages, and silvicultural practices) is essential for this role. The project will be carried out in a collaborative environment between the two research groups, providing extensive technical support and interdisciplinary expertise in ecohydrology and forest management. Job description The doctoral project focuses on assessing the resilience of Swiss drinking water resources to forest changes and management interventions. As the successful candidate, your work will include:
• National-Scale Data Integration: Analyzing gradients in forest cover and structure (e.g., tree species mixtures, density) in relation to long-term drinking water parameters, accounting for hydrogeology and land-use history
• Field Monitoring & Sampling: Conducting water quality assessments across Swiss-wide spring networks to identify how management practices influence resilience during event-driven disturbances
• Mechanistic Investigations: Monitoring intensively instrumented experimental sites to determine how forest health and structure alter subsurface flow routing and contamination pulses
• Synthesis & Strategy Development: Developing and evaluating suitable management strategies to reduce drinking water risks
• Stakeholder Communication: Performing statistical analyses and modeling to translate findings into actionable management recommendations for water abstractions The full-time position is funded for four years. Salary and social benefits are provided according to ETH Zurich rules. Profile Upon starting, you must have completed a Master’s degree in hydrology, environmental sciences, forest sciences, ecology, or a closely related field with experience in water chemistry, silviculture, experimental field work and large-scale data analysis. You must have good statistical skills and programming experience (e.g., in R or Python). Excellent written and spoken English, as well as a driver’s license, are mandatory. For this project, we consider German and other Swiss national languages an asset. Good writing skills and the ability to work in an interdisciplinary environment are expected. Workplace Workplace We offer
• An inspiring, international, and interdisciplinary work environment in a world-leading research institute

Le groupe d'écohydrologie WaldLab fait partie de la chaire d'hydrologie et de sciences du système fluvial de l'ETH Zurich Institute of Environmental Engineering, avec une expertise dans les évaluations de la chimie de l'eau dans les écosystèmes forestiers. Le groupe Silviculture fait partie de la Chaire de gestion des ressources forestières de l'ETH Zurich Institute of Terrestrial Ecosystems, avec une expertise en sylviculture et en gestion forestière. Nous sommes à la recherche d'un doctorant fiable, enthousiaste et très motivé, passionné de sciences interdisciplinaires pour rejoindre notre équipe. Contexte du projet Ce poste fait partie du projet « Gestion des forêts et sécurité de l'eau potable dans le cadre du changement climatique » soutenu par l'Office fédéral de l'environnement. Le projet étudie le lien critique entre la gestion des écosystèmes forestiers et la santé et la qualité de l'eau potable dans toute la Suisse. À mesure que le changement climatique intensifie les perturbations comme les sécheresses, les vents et les épidémies de ravageurs, il est essentiel de comprendre comment la structure et la gestion des forêts influent sur la qualité de l'eau. À l'échelle nationale et sur des sites expérimentaux, le projet intègre l'analyse des données à l'échelle nationale, la surveillance de la qualité de l'eau des réseaux printaniers et un aperçu mécaniste détaillé de l'acheminement des flux souterrains et des temps de transit. Le projet est étroitement aligné sur les parties prenantes et les autorités décisionnelles des forêts et de l'eau potable; une compréhension solide et fondamentale des écosystèmes forestiers d'Europe centrale et suisse (comprenant la composition des espèces, les étapes de développement et les pratiques sylvicoles) est donc essentielle pour ce rôle. Le projet sera réalisé dans un environnement de collaboration entre les deux groupes de recherche, fournissant un soutien technique étendu et une expertise interdisciplinaire en écohydrologie et en gestion forestière. Description du poste Le projet doctoral vise à évaluer la résilience des ressources en eau potable suisses aux changements forestiers et aux interventions de gestion. En tant que candidat reçu, votre travail comprendra :
• Intégration des données à l'échelle nationale: analyse des gradients du couvert et de la structure des forêts (par exemple, mélanges d'espèces d'arbres, densité) par rapport aux paramètres à long terme de l'eau potable, tenant compte de l'hydrogéologie et de l'historique de l'utilisation des terres
• Surveillance et échantillonnage sur le terrain: réalisation d'évaluations de la qualité de l'eau dans les réseaux printaniers à l'échelle suisse pour déterminer comment les pratiques de gestion influent sur la résilience pendant les perturbations provoquées par les événements
• Enquêtes mécanistes: surveillance intensive des sites expérimentaux pour déterminer comment la santé et la structure des forêts modifient l'écoulement souterrain et les impulsions de contamination
• Synthèse et élaboration de stratégies : élaborer et évaluer des stratégies de gestion appropriées pour réduire les risques liés à l'eau potable
• Communication des parties prenantes: réaliser des analyses statistiques et des modélisations pour traduire les résultats en recommandations de gestion applicables aux prélèvements d'eau Le poste à temps plein est financé pour quatre ans. Les salaires et les prestations sociales sont fournis conformément aux règles de Zurich. Postdoc in Resilient Satellite Navigation (GNSS) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken Are you passionate about advancing the frontiers of resilient navigation to tackle the growing challenges of signal interference? Are you an expert in GNSS processing, eager to integrate cutting-edge multi-sensor fusion and AI technologies? Join our young and dynamic team at the Chair of Space Geodesy , led by Prof. Benedikt Soja . We are at the forefront of developing innovative methods for space- and ground-based geodetic and navigation applications, with the goal of enabling high-precision, continuous, and real-time positioning. Our team has gained prominence for our work in applying machine learning to PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) and geomonitoring challenges, including signal characterization and anomaly detection. Project background We are looking for a highly motivated researcher to lead our efforts in Resilient Navigation. As global reliance on GNSS grows, so does the need for systems that can withstand jamming, spoofing, and complex environments. This position focuses on developing next-generation navigation software and multi-sensor fusion strategies to ensure precision and reliability in challenging scenarios. Job description The successful candidate will lead GNSS-based research within our group and support existing projects related to GNSS and PNT. Key responsibilities include:
• Software Development: Developing GNSS software using Factor Graph Optimization (FGO) based on existing open-source software packages
• Sensor Fusion: Implementing multi-sensor fusion strategies
• Resilience: Advancing real-time GNSS processing with a primary focus on the detection, characterization, and mitigation of jamming and spoofing scenarios
• AI Integration: Exploring the integration of AI/ML concepts to enhance navigation resilience together with other group members
• Hardware & Simulation: Working with both high-grade and low-cost GNSS equipment and utilizing a GNSS signal simulator (Spirent)
• Academic Leadership: Leading and co-authoring high-impact publications and participating in the preparation of grant applications
• Teaching & Supervision: Supporting the lectures "GNSS" and "Navigation" (full course materials exist) and contributing to the supervision of PhD and Master students Profile Required Experience:
• PhD in Geodesy, Geomatics, Aerospace Engineering, Signal Processing, or a related field

• Very good programming skills (e.g., Python, C++)
• Fluency in English People Skills & Attributes:
• Strong analytical mindset with hands-on problem-solving abilities
• Comfortable working in interdisciplinary teams
• Self-motivated, structured, and curious about emerging AI technologies Advantageous:
• Experience with Factor Graph Optimization, multi-sensor fusion methods, or AI/ML applications
• CH/EU/EFTA citizenship or a valid Swiss work permit
• Proficiency in German Workplace Workplace We offer
• Unique access to high-grade and low-cost GNSS networks in Switzerland and beyond

• A supportive and inclusive work environment that fosters professional growth and development

• Salary and benefits according to ETH Zurich standards

Êtes-vous un expert en traitement GNSS, désireux d'intégrer les technologies de fusion multicapteurs et d'IA de pointe? Rejoignez notre équipe jeune et dynamique à la chaire de géodésie spatiale, dirigée par le Prof. Benedikt Soja . Au fur et à mesure que se développe la dépendance mondiale à l'égard du GNSS, le besoin de systèmes capables de résister au brouillage, à l'effusion et aux environnements complexes se fait sentir. Cette position met l'accent sur le développement de logiciels de navigation de nouvelle génération et de stratégies de fusion multicapteurs pour assurer la précision et la fiabilité dans les scénarios difficiles. • Développement de logiciels: développement de logiciels GNSS en utilisant Factor Graph Optimization (FGO) basé sur les logiciels open-source existants
• Fusion de capteurs : mise en œuvre de stratégies de fusion multicapteurs
• Résilience : Faire progresser le traitement en temps réel des GNSS en mettant l'accent sur la détection, la caractérisation et l'atténuation des scénarios de brouillage et de spoofing
• Intégration de l'IA : explorer l'intégration des concepts d'IA/ML pour améliorer la résilience de la navigation avec d'autres membres du groupe

Descrizione Operazioni di Sistemi Leader di Gruppo 80%-100%, Zurigo, permanente stampa Druppo La piattaforma tecnologica ETH Zurich NEXUS Personalized Health consente la scoperta e la ricerca traduttiva per la salute personalizzata. Offriamo una vasta gamma di competenze tra Bioinformatica clinica, Biostatistica, Ingegneria Software, Operazioni Sistemi e Screening & Lab Automation. Le Operazioni di Sistemi colmano il divario tra i sistemi di costruzione e li fanno funzionare in modo affidabile nella ricerca del mondo reale e nei contesti clinici. Il team ha attualmente 5 membri ed è intenzionalmente diversificato, tra cui l'ingegneria dell'affidabilità del sito e i profili operativi coinvolti nell'esecuzione di studi clinici. Il gruppo prende tipicamente il sopravvento del lavoro come sistemi maturati dallo sviluppo nell'uso del mondo reale, e raccoglie anche le priorità operative che si presentano in NEXUS. Mansioni
• leadership di squadra: guida, mentore e sviluppare un team diverso con diversi background professionali e modi di lavorare.
• Proprietà operativa: assumersi la responsabilità per il funzionamento affidabile di sistemi interni e partner entro un ambito concordato, tra cui distribuzioni, ambienti, modelli di accesso e stabilità quotidiana.
• Gestione del ciclo di vita e della transizione: definire e eseguire gli avanzi dallo sviluppo in fasi di test controllate e funzionamento a più lungo termine, inclusi i criteri di accettazione, la documentazione e i confini di proprietà.
• Esecuzione regolamentata e strutturata: lavoro coordinato che richiede consapevolezza normativa, vincoli di certificazione, processi convalidati o documentazione rigorosa, per esempio nelle impostazioni di studio clinico.
• Gestione degli stakeholder e delle aspettative: gestire proattivamente le aspettative, risolvere i conflitti presto, e tradurre tra realtà tecniche e esigenze degli utenti, impedendo incomprensioni di trasformarsi in escalation.
• Consegna del servizio e priorità: assunzione, triage e priorità in più richieste parallele, equilibratura dell'urgenza, del rischio e del valore con il processo decisionale trasparente.
• Pratiche di affidabilità: stabilire standard pragmatici per il monitoraggio, i backup, la gestione dei cambiamenti e il controllo degli accessi. Questo ruolo non richiede on-call, ma richiede la proprietà e la prevedibilità.
• Collaborazione trasversale: lavorare a stretto contatto con Software Engineering, Bioinformatica clinica, Biostatistica e Screening & Lab Automation per mantenere coerente la consegna end-to-end.
• Miglioramento del processo: semplificare e standardizzare dove aiuta, senza creare burocrazia.
• Gestione delle risorse: capacità di piano, priorità e reporting per il gruppo attraverso un portafoglio crescente di impegni operativi. Controllo automatico rapido Si prospererà in questo ruolo se:
• Ti piace stabilizzare, operare e migliorare continuamente i sistemi nel tempo - non solo la costruzione di soluzioni greenfield.
• Crea chiarezza, tranquillità e affidabilità in ambienti di stakeholder complessi.
• È comodo navigare conversazioni difficili, conflitti, e l'escalation, e può risolverli costruttivamente.
• Si chiarisce proattivamente la proprietà e sono disposti a definire e far rispettare quando necessario.
• Unisci la profondità tecnica alle competenze delle persone forti e all'esecuzione strutturata.
• Ti piace guidare con responsabilità sia per le persone che per i risultati dei servizi, non solo la consegna tecnica.
• Ti piace costruire processi operativi che riducono l'attrito senza introdurre burocrazia inutile.
• Sei a tuo agio a lavorare su diversi profili, dagli ingegneri alle operazioni cliniche e da altri stakeholder non tecnici. Profilo Non negoziabili:

descriptionByLocale.en:
Group Leader Systems Operations 80%-100%, Zurich, permanent print Drucken The ETH Zurich technology platform NEXUS Personalized Health enables discovery and translational research for personalized health. We offer a broad range of expertise across Clinical Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Software Engineering, Systems Operations, and Screening & Lab Automation. Systems Operations bridges the gap between building systems and making them run reliably in real-world research and clinical contexts. The team currently has 5 members and is intentionally diverse, spanning roles such as site reliability engineering as well as operational profiles involved in clinical study execution. The group typically takes over work as systems mature from development into real-world use, and it also picks up operational priorities that arise across NEXUS. Job description As Group Leader Systems Operations, you lead a diverse team and define how NEXUS operates systems for itself and together with users and partners. You create clarity across responsibilities, reduce friction, and establish predictable service delivery that enables projects to succeed in practice.
• Team leadership: lead, mentor, and develop a diverse team with different professional backgrounds and ways of working.
• Operational ownership: take responsibility for the reliable operation of internal and partner-facing systems within an agreed scope, including deployments, environments, access patterns, and day-to-day stability.
• Transition and lifecycle management: define and run handovers from development into controlled test phases and longer-running operation, including acceptance criteria, documentation, and ownership boundaries.
• Regulated and structured execution: coordinate work that requires regulatory awareness, certification constraints, validated processes, or strict documentation, for example in clinical study settings.
• Stakeholder and expectation management: proactively manage expectations, resolve conflicts early, and translate between technical realities and user needs, preventing misunderstandings from turning into escalations.
• Service delivery and prioritization: run intake, triage, and prioritization across multiple parallel demands, balancing urgency, risk, and value with transparent decision-making.
• Reliability practices: establish pragmatic standards for monitoring, backups, change management, and access control. This role does not require on-call, but it does require ownership and predictability.
• Cross-team collaboration: work closely with Software Engineering, Clinical Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, and Screening & Lab Automation to keep end-to-end delivery coherent.
• Process improvement: simplify and standardize where it helps, without creating bureaucracy.
• Resource management: plan capacity, priorities, and reporting for the group across a growing portfolio of operational commitments. Quick Self-Check You will thrive in this role if:
• You enjoy stabilising, operating, and continuously improving systems over time - not just building greenfield solutions.
• You create clarity, calm, and reliability in complex stakeholder environments.
• You are comfortable navigating difficult conversations, conflict, and escalation, and can resolve them constructively.
• You proactively clarify ownership and are willing to define and enforce it when needed.
• You combine technical depth with strong people skills and structured execution.
• You enjoy leading with responsibility for both people and service outcomes, not just technical delivery.
• You like building operational processes that reduce friction without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.
• You are comfortable working across diverse profiles, from engineers to clinical operations and other non-technical stakeholders. Profile Non-Negotiables:
• Proven leadership experience in operations, platform engineering, site reliability, clinical operations, or comparable roles with deliver

Descrizione Chef de groupe Opérations de systèmes 80%-100%, Zurich, permanente imprimer Drucken La plateforme technologique ETH Zurich NEXUS Personalized Health permet la découverte et la recherche translationnelle pour une santé personnalisée. Nous offrons une large gamme d'expertise dans la bioinformatique clinique, la biostatistique, le génie logiciel, l'exploitation des systèmes et le dépistage et l'automatisation des laboratoires. L'exploitation des systèmes permet de combler l'écart entre les systèmes de construction et de les faire fonctionner de manière fiable dans des contextes réels de recherche et cliniques. À l'heure actuelle, l'équipe compte cinq membres et est intentionnellement diversifiée, ce qui englobe des rôles tels que l'ingénierie de la fiabilité du site et les profils opérationnels associés à l'exécution des études cliniques. En général, le groupe reprend le travail à mesure que les systèmes arrivent à maturité, du développement à l'utilisation réelle, et il reprend également les priorités opérationnelles qui se présentent dans NEXUS. Mansioni
• La direction de l'équipe : dirigez, mentorez et développez une équipe diversifiée ayant différents antécédents professionnels et différentes façons de travailler.
• Prise en charge opérationnelle: prendre en charge le fonctionnement fiable des systèmes internes et des systèmes faisant face aux partenaires dans un cadre convenu, y compris les déploiements, les environnements, les schémas d'accès et la stabilité quotidienne.
• Gestion de la transition et du cycle de vie: définir et passer du développement aux phases d'essai contrôlées et à l'opération à plus long terme, y compris les critères d'acceptation, la documentation et les limites de propriété.
• Exécution réglementée et structurée : coordonner les travaux qui nécessitent une sensibilisation réglementaire, des contraintes en matière de certification, des processus validés ou une documentation stricte, par exemple dans le cadre d'études cliniques.
• Gestion des parties prenantes et des attentes: gérer les attentes de manière proactive, résoudre les conflits rapidement et traduire entre les réalités techniques et les besoins des utilisateurs, en empêchant les malentendus de se transformer en escalades.
• Prestation des services et hiérarchisation des priorités : exécuter l'admission, le tri et l'établissement des priorités sur plusieurs demandes parallèles, équilibrer l'urgence, les risques et la valeur avec la transparence des décisions.
• Pratiques de fiabilité : établir des normes pragmatiques pour le suivi, les sauvegardes, la gestion du changement et le contrôle d'accès. Ce rôle n'exige pas un appel, mais il exige la propriété et la prévisibilité.
• Collaboration intersectorielle : travailler en étroite collaboration avec le génie logiciel, la bioinformatique clinique, la biostatistique et le dépistage et l'automatisation des laboratoires afin de maintenir la cohérence de la prestation de bout en bout.
• Amélioration des processus : simplifier et normaliser l'endroit où elle aide, sans créer de bureaucratie.
• Gestion des ressources : planification de la capacité, des priorités et de l'établissement de rapports pour le groupe dans un portefeuille croissant d'engagements opérationnels. Vérification rapide Vous prospérerez dans ce rôle si :
• Vous aimez la stabilisation, le fonctionnement et l'amélioration continue des systèmes au fil du temps - pas seulement la construction de solutions de terrain vert.
• Vous créez la clarté, le calme et la fiabilité dans des environnements d'intervenants complexes.
• Vous êtes à l'aise de naviguer dans des conversations difficiles, des conflits et une escalade, et vous pouvez les résoudre de manière constructive.
• Vous clarifiez de manière proactive la propriété et êtes prêt à la définir et à la faire respecter au besoin.
• Vous combinez profondeur technique, compétences humaines fortes et exécution structurée.
• Vous aimez diriger avec responsabilité pour les personnes et les résultats de service, pas seulement la prestation technique.
• Vous aimez construire des processus opérationnels qui réduisent les frictions sans introduire une bureaucratie inutile.
• Vous êtes à l'aise de travailler à travers différents profils, des ingénieurs aux opérations cliniques et autres acteurs non techniques. Profil Non négociables:
• Expérience éprouvée de leadership dans les opérations, l'ingénierie des plateformes, la fiabilité du site, les opérations cliniques ou des rôles comparables avec la prestation

Il candidato di successo si unirà a uno sforzo interdisciplinare sviluppando tecnologie diagnostiche innovative basate su sequenziamento lungo e analisi di sequenza in tempo reale. Sfondo del progetto L'identificazione rapida e accurata delle infezioni batteriche rimane una grande sfida nella pratica clinica, in particolare nelle impostazioni di emergenza in cui la diagnosi ritardata può portare a trattamento suboptimale o ritardato e ad una maggiore mortalità in condizioni come la sepsi. I metodi diagnostici attuali spesso richiedono 24–72 ore, che possono contribuire all'uso empirico di antibiotici ad ampio spettro e all'emergere di resistenza antimicrobica. Il progetto integra competenze sperimentali e computazionali per consentire l'analisi delle sequenze in tempo reale e fornire risultati clinicamente attuabili entro ore. Descrizione del lavoro - svilupperai e implementerai nuovi metodi computazionali per l'analisi dei dati di sequenziamento lungo, tra cui analisi pre- e post-base-calling, per supportare lo sviluppo di una piattaforma diagnostica di nuova generazione - Progetterai algoritmi e modelli statistici per l'analisi in tempo reale delle sequenze di dati transcriptomici host e patogeni, con un focus su approcci robusti e scalabili per applicazioni cliniche - Si lavorerà a stretto contatto con un team interdisciplinare di bioinformatica, microbiologi, medici e ingegneri in tutta l'ETH di Zurigo, l'Università di Zurigo, e l'Ospedale Universitario di Zurigo - Contribuirai all'integrazione dei metodi di bioinformatica in un progetto di ricerca traduttiva volto a consentire la diagnostica rapida e clinica delle malattie infettive - Condurrai progetti di ricerca computazionale, pubblicherai risultati in importanti riviste scientifiche e contribuirai ad avanzare metodi in genomica microbica, analisi di sequenziamento a lungo termine e biologia computazionale applicata Profilo Si dovrebbe avere una laurea in: - Biologia computazionale / Bioinformatica - Scienza informatica - Statistiche / Matematica applicata - o un campo quantitativo correlato con un forte background in algoritmi, strutture di dati e modellazione statistica. Postdoctoral Researcher - Bioinformatics 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Clinical Genomics team led by Dr. André Kahles at the Biomedical Informatics Lab (BMI Lab), headed by Prof. Gunnar Rätsch, at ETH Zurich, is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher with a strong background in sequence bioinformatics, algorithms and data structures. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary effort developing innovative diagnostic technologies based on long-read sequencing and real-time sequence analysis. Project background Rapid and accurate identification of bacterial infections remains a major challenge in clinical practice, particularly in emergency settings where delayed diagnosis can lead to suboptimal or delayed treatment and increased mortality in conditions such as sepsis. Current diagnostic methods often require 24–72 hours, which can contribute to the empirical use of broad-spectrum antibiotics and the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. Within the RADIANT-Dx consortium, our interdisciplinary team is developing a portable diagnostic platform based on long-read sequencing to enable rapid transcriptomic profiling of host responses and pathogens directly from blood samples. The project integrates experimental and computational expertise to enable real-time sequence analysis and deliver clinically actionable results within hours. Job description
• You will develop and implement novel computational methods for the analysis of long-read sequencing data, including both pre– and post–base-calling analysis, to support the development of a next-generation diagnostic platform
• You will design algorithms and statistical models for real-time sequence analysis of host and pathogen transcriptomic data, with a focus on robust and scalable approaches for clinical applications
• You will work closely with an interdisciplinary team of bioinformaticians, microbiologists, clinicians, and engineers across ETH Zurich, the University of Zurich, and the University Hospital Zurich
• You will contribute to the integration of bioinformatics methods into a translational research project aimed at enabling rapid and clinically actionable infectious disease diagnostics
• You will lead computational research projects, publish results in leading scientific journals, and contribute to advancing methods in microbial genomics, long-read sequencing analysis, and applied computational biology Profile You should have a PhD degree in:
• Computational Biology / Bioinformatics
• Computer Science
• Statistics / Applied Mathematics
• or a related quantitative field with a strong background in algorithms, data structures, and statistical modeling. Experience in sequence analysis, microbial genomics, and long-read sequencing data analysis is highly desirable. Familiarity with signal processing or applied machine learning is advantageous. You should demonstrate strong motivation to develop innovative computational methods and to contribute to interdisciplinary research with potential clinical impact, ideally supported by a solid publication record.
