Descrizione Chercheur postdoctoral - Bioinformatique 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken L'équipe de génomique clinique dirigée par le Dr André Kahles au Laboratoire d'informatique biomédicale (BMI Lab), dirigée par le Prof. Gunnar Rätsch, à l'ETH Zurich, cherche un chercheur postdoctoral hautement motivé avec une solide expérience en bioinformatique séquence, algorithmes et structures de données. Le candidat retenu s'associera à un effort interdisciplinaire visant à mettre au point des technologies diagnostiques novatrices fondées sur le séquençage à longue distance et l'analyse des séquences en temps réel. Contexte du projet L'identification rapide et précise des infections bactériennes demeure un défi majeur dans la pratique clinique, en particulier dans les situations d'urgence où un diagnostic retardé peut conduire à un traitement sous-optimal ou retardé et une mortalité accrue dans des conditions telles que la septicémie. Les méthodes diagnostiques actuelles nécessitent souvent de 24 à 72 heures, ce qui peut contribuer à l'utilisation empirique d'antibiotiques à large spectre et à l'émergence d'une résistance antimicrobienne. Au sein du consortium RADIANT-Dx, notre équipe interdisciplinaire développe une plate-forme de diagnostic portable basée sur le séquençage de longue durée pour permettre un profil transcriptomique rapide des réponses des hôtes et des pathogènes directement à partir d'échantillons sanguins. Le projet intègre une expertise expérimentale et computationnelle pour permettre l'analyse en temps réel des séquences et produire des résultats cliniquement exploitables en quelques heures. Description du poste - Vous allez développer et mettre en œuvre de nouvelles méthodes de calcul pour l'analyse des données de séquençage à lecture longue, y compris l'analyse pré- et post-appel de base, afin de soutenir le développement d'une plateforme diagnostique de prochaine génération - Vous concevrez des algorithmes et des modèles statistiques pour l'analyse en temps réel des séquences des données transcriptomiques de l'hôte et du pathogène, en mettant l'accent sur des approches robustes et évolutives pour les applications cliniques - Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec une équipe interdisciplinaire de bioinformaticiens, de microbiologistes, de cliniciens et d'ingénieurs à travers l'ETH Zurich, l'Université de Zurich et l'Hôpital Universitaire Zurich - Vous contribuerez à l'intégration des méthodes bioinformatiques dans un projet de recherche translationnelle visant à permettre un diagnostic rapide et cliniquement réalisable des maladies infectieuses - Vous dirigerez des projets de recherche computationnelle, publierez les résultats dans des revues scientifiques de premier plan et contribuerez à l'avancement des méthodes de génomique microbienne, à l'analyse de séquençage des lectures longues et à la biologie computationnelle appliquée Profil Vous devriez avoir un doctorat en: - Biologie computationnelle / Bioinformatique - Informatique - Statistiques / Mathématiques appliquées - ou un domaine quantitatif connexe avec une solide connaissance des algorithmes, des structures de données et de la modélisation statistique. L'expérience dans l'analyse des séquences, la génomique microbienne et l'analyse des données de séquençage des lis longs est hautement souhaitable. La connaissance avec le traitement des signaux ou l'apprentissage automatique appliqué est avantageuse. Vous devez faire preuve d'une forte motivation à développer des méthodes informatiques novatrices et à contribuer à la recherche interdisciplinaire ayant un impact clinique potentiel, idéalement appuyée par un dossier de publication solide. descriptionByLocale.it:
Due studenti di dottorato in ecofisiologia vegetale e servizi ecosistemici di miscele di colture (Progetto: PhenoMix) 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Entrambe le posizioni fanno parte del progetto “ PhenoMix: fenotipazione multidimensionale del campo delle miscele di colture”, sostenuto dalla Fondazione svizzera per la scienza nazionale. PhenoMix affronta diversi aspetti delle miscele di legume-cereali agroecologicamente vantaggiose nel campo. Due dei quattro dottorandi sono ospitati dal gruppo Grassland Sciences all'ETH di Zurigo. La ricerca del nostro gruppo si concentra sul processo- e il sistema-comprensione della biosfera - scambio di gas serra atmosfera, ecofisiologia vegetale, e servizi ecosistemici di agroecosistemi e applicazioni isotopi stabili per studiare la diversità funzionale degli impianti. Il gruppo Grassland Sciences è un gruppo di lavoro vibrante e internazionale nel Dipartimento di Scienze dei Sistemi Ambientali dell'ETH di Zurigo. Stiamo cercando due studenti medici affidabili, entusiasti e altamente motivati con una passione per la scienza per unirsi alla nostra squadra. Sfondo del progetto Le due posizioni di dottorato fanno parte di PhenoMix , un progetto congiunto all'ETH di Zurigo, al Centro svizzero per la scienza dei dati e all'Agroscope. PhenoMix si concentra sulle miscele legume-cereali, cioè diverse varietà di piselli e lenticchie, nonché grano, avena, e orzo coltivato sotto una piattaforma di fenotipazione di campo sperimentale e su un campo adiacente. Diversi pacchetti di lavoro affrontano la fenotyping, ecofisiologia vegetale, scienza dei dati e valutazioni agro-economiche. I due studenti di dottorato nel nostro pacchetto di lavoro valuteranno le differenze nel microclima a baldacchino e nei tratti vegetali, nonché i servizi ecosistemici tra stand puri e miscele di colture. Sulla base di applicazioni stabili di carbonio, azoto e isotopo dell'acqua, determineranno la luce, l'azoto e l'uso dell'acqua e valuteranno la complementarità nelle miscele delle colture durante tre stagioni di ritaglio. Descrizione del lavoro I due progetti di dottorato si concentrano sul microclima a baldacchino, sui tratti vegetali, sull'uso delle risorse, sui servizi ecosistemici e sulla complementarità dei legumi e delle colture cerealicole coltivate in stand e miscele puri. Il focus di entrambi i singoli progetti di dottorato dipenderà dalle competenze e dagli interessi esistenti. Le attività generali includono:
• Misure di microclima a baldacchino, architettura a baldacchino (ad esempio, altezza, indice di superficie fogliare), caratteristiche vegetali e produzione di biomassa per valutare l'uso di luce e spazio delle colture,

Two doctoral students in plant ecophysiology and ecosystem services of crop mixtures (Project: PhenoMix) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken Both positions are part of the project “ PhenoMix : Multidimensional field phenotyping of crop mixtures”, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation. PhenoMix addresses different aspects of agroecologically beneficial legume-cereal crop mixtures in the field. Two of the four doctoral students are hosted by the Grassland Sciences group at ETH Zurich. Our group’s research focuses on the process- and system-understanding of biosphere‒atmosphere greenhouse gas exchange, plant ecophysiology, and ecosystem services of agroecosystems as well as stable isotope applications to study plant functional diversity. The Grassland Sciences group is a vibrant and international working group in the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich. We are looking for two reliable, enthusiastic, and highly motivated doctoral students with a passion for science to join our team. Project background The two doctoral positions are part of PhenoMix , a joint project at ETH Zurich, the Swiss Data Science Center, and Agroscope. PhenoMix focuses on legume-cereal mixtures, i.e., different varieties of pea and lentil as well as wheat, oats, and barley grown under an experimental field phenotyping platform and on a neighbouring field. Different Work Packages address phenotyping, plant ecophysiology, data science, and agro-economic assessments. The two doctoral students in our Work Package will assess differences in canopy microclimate and plant traits as well as ecosystem services between pure stands and crop mixtures. Based on stable carbon, nitrogen, and water isotope applications, they will determine light, nitrogen, and water use and assess complementarity in crop mixtures during three cropping seasons. Job description The two doctoral projects focus on canopy microclimate, plant traits, resource use, ecosystem services as well as complementarity of legumes and cereal crops grown in pure stands and mixtures. The focus of both individual doctoral projects will depend on existing skills and interest. Overall tasks include:
• Measurements of canopy microclimate, canopy architecture (e.g., height, leaf area index), plant traits, and biomass production to assess crop light and space use,
• Measurements of soil resource supply and plant sampling for stable isotope analyses to assess crop nitrogen and water use
• Quantification of litter decomposition, leaching, weed pressure, and yield quality to assess ecosystem services
• Evaluation of plant phenotyping models, jointly with the other Work Packages of PhenoMix
• Statistical analyses, including machine learning approaches
• Presentation at national and international events as well as publication

Deux doctorants en écophysiologie végétale et services écosystémiques de mélanges de cultures (Projet: PhénoMix) 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Les deux positions s'inscrivent dans le projet PhénoMix : Phénotypage multidimensionnel sur le terrain des mélanges de cultures, soutenu par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences. PhénoMix aborde différents aspects des mélanges agroécologiquement bénéfiques de légumineuses et de céréales sur le terrain. Deux des quatre doctorants sont accueillis par le groupe des sciences de Grassland à l'ETH Zurich. Notre recherche de groupe porte sur la compréhension des processus et des systèmes de l'échange de gaz à effet de serre de la biosphère–atmosphère, de l'écophysiologie des plantes et des services écosystémiques des agroécosystèmes ainsi que des applications isotopiques stables pour étudier la diversité fonctionnelle des plantes. Le groupe Grassland Sciences est un groupe de travail dynamique et international au Département des sciences des systèmes environnementaux de Zurich. Nous sommes à la recherche de deux doctorants fiables, enthousiastes et très motivés, passionnés de sciences, pour rejoindre notre équipe. PhénoMix se concentre sur les mélanges légumineuses-céréales, c'est-à-dire différentes variétés de pois et de lentilles ainsi que le blé, l'avoine et l'orge cultivés sous une plate-forme de phénotypage expérimentale au champ et sur un champ voisin. PhD position in Crop Phenotyping (PhenoMix project) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken This doctoral student position is part of the project “ PhenoMix: Multidimensional field phenotyping of crop mixtures ”, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation. The position is hosted by the Crop Science group ; a vibrant and interdisciplinary working group in the Institute of Agricultural Sciences at the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich. Our group’s phenotyping research focuses on the development of methods and models to determine traits of relevance for crop breeding and variety testing. Project background PhenoMix is a joint project of four research groups at ETH Zurich, the Swiss Data Science Center and Agroscope. The overall objective of PhenoMix is to test the hypothesis that current high throughput field phenotyping (HTFP) technology in combination with plant physiological assessments and data science can provide a breakthrough to determine genotypes that can be successfully combined in agroecologically beneficial legume-cereal mixtures. Different varieties of pea and lentil as well as wheat, oats and barley will be grown under our field phenotyping platform FIP ( FIP – Crop Science | ETH Zurich ), on a neighbouring experimental field and on farmer’s fields. PhenoMix Work Packages address phenotyping, plant ecophysiology, data science, and agro-economic assessments with four doctoral students, two postdocs and several technicians assigned to those work packages. The Crop Phenotyping doctoral student will contribute to collecting HTFP data, improving phenotyping workflows and developing a field robot for lean phenotyping. Job description This doctoral project will form an important cornerstone in the mosaic of the entire project with specific tasks depending on skills, interests and alignment with at least two postdoctoral projects for which recruiting is also going on currently. Overall tasks of the project include:
• Collection of HTFP data from various phenotyping devices such as the FIP (multi-view RGB imaging), drones, handheld and manual devices
• Contribution to the design and/or establishment of a phenotyping robot that can acquire data from RGB cameras and potentially other sensors
• Improving phenotyping workflows and models to extract traits such as canopy height, canopy cover, tillering, reflectance, senescence or growth dynamics from this data
• Performing statistical analyses, including AI-based approaches
• Presentation of results at national and international events and publication in peer-reviewed journals
• Assistance in plot establishment, maintenance, and harvest across all Work Packages of PhenoMix. Profile

L'objectif global de PhenoMix est de tester l'hypothèse selon laquelle la technologie actuelle de phénotypage en champ à haut débit, combinée à des évaluations physiologiques des plantes et à la science des données, peut fournir une percée pour déterminer les génotypes qui peuvent être combinés avec succès dans des mélanges agroécologiquement bénéfiques légumineuses-céréales. Différentes variétés de pois et de lentilles ainsi que de blé, d'avoine et d'orge seront cultivées sous notre plateforme de phénotypage de champ FIP (FIP – Crop Science) et sur un champ expérimental voisin et sur des champs fermiers. Les trousses de travail PhénoMix traitent du phénotypage, de l'écophysiologie des plantes, de la science des données et des évaluations agro-économiques avec quatre doctorants, deux postdoctorants et plusieurs techniciens affectés à ces trousses de travail. Le doctorant Crop Phénotyping contribuera à la collecte des données du PFTE, à l'amélioration des flux de travail du phénotypage et au développement d'un robot de terrain pour le phénotypage maigre. Questa posizione è ospitata dal gruppo Crop Science; un gruppo di lavoro vibrante e interdisciplinare nell'Istituto di Scienze Agrarie presso il Dipartimento di Scienze Ambientali dell'ETH di Zurigo. La ricerca fenotipante del nostro gruppo si concentra sullo sviluppo di metodi e modelli per determinare i tratti di rilevanza per l'allevamento di colture e test di varietà. Il progetto PhenoMix è un progetto congiunto di quattro gruppi di ricerca all'ETH di Zurigo, al Centro svizzero per la scienza dei dati e all'Agroscope. L'obiettivo generale di PhenoMix è quello di testare l'ipotesi che l'attuale tecnologia di fenotipazione del campo ad alto rendimento (HTFP) in combinazione con le valutazioni fisiologiche delle piante e la scienza dei dati può fornire una svolta per determinare genotipi che possono essere combinati con successo in miscele legume-cere agroecologicamente vantaggiose. descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoc position in Phenotyping of Crop Mixtures (PhenoMix project) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken This postdoctoral position is part of the project “ PhenoMix: Multidimensional field phenotyping of crop mixtures ”, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation. This position is hosted by the Crop Science group ; a vibrant and interdisciplinary working group in the Institute of Agricultural Sciences at the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich. Our group’s phenotyping research focuses on the development of methods and models to determine traits of relevance for crop breeding and variety testing. Project background PhenoMix is a joint project of four research groups at ETH Zurich, the Swiss Data Science Center and Agroscope. The overall objective of PhenoMix is to test the hypothesis that current high throughput field phenotyping (HTFP) technology in combination with plant physiological assessments and data science can provide a breakthrough to determine genotypes that can be successfully combined in agroecologically beneficial legume-cereal mixtures. Different varieties of pea and lentil as well as wheat, oats and barley will be grown under our field phenotyping platform FIP , on a neighbouring experimental field and on farmer’s fields. PhenoMix Work Packages address phenotyping, plant ecophysiology, data science, and agro-economic assessments with four doctoral students, two postdocs and several technicians assigned to those work packages. The postdoc for Phenotyping of Crop Mixtures will coordinate several overarching activities in the PhenoMix project and will contribute to collecting HTFP data, improving phenotyping workflows and developing a field robot for lean phenotyping. Job description This postdoctoral position will form an important cornerstone in the mosaic of the entire project with specific tasks depending on skills, interests and alignment with at least one other postdoctoral position on data science and a doctoral student on Crop Phenotyping within the Crop Science group, for which recruiting is also going on currently. Overall tasks of this project include:
• Co-design and coordinate field experiments and workplan for HTFP data collection
• Contribute to field work and to the collection of HTFP data from various phenotyping devices such as the FIP (multi-view RGB imaging), drones, handheld and manual devices
• Contribute to the design and/or establishment of a phenotyping robot that can acquire data from RGB cameras and potentially other sensors
• Generate modelling approaches to predict optimal cereal-legume combinations
• Supervise and mentor students from BSc to PhD-level
• Assist in the delivery of lectures or seminars for the Crop Science group
• Publish results in peer-reviewed journals; present at national and international conferences
• Contribute to international research networks and apply for funding
• The initial contract duration is two years with the possibility of extension to the full lifetime of this four-year-project, based on satisfactory performance
• Salary and social benefits are provided according to ETH Zurich rules Profile
• A PhD in agricultural sciences or a related field
• Several years of research experience in field crop phenotyping
• Good statistical and programming skills (e.g. in R or Python)
• Evidence of research excellence through peer-reviewed publications
• A strong desire for teaching, mentoring, teamwork and team coordination
• Driver’s license
• Good oral communication skills in German are highly beneficial Workplace Workplace We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society
• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

Postdoctoral Researcher - OCCL 100%, Singapore, fixed-term Drucken The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions. Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) . The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems. Project background The current era of artificial intelligence is predominantly driven by advances in computational power and infrastructure. As models scale to unprecedented sizes, their capabilities are enhanced through strategies such as reinforcement learning (RL) and innovative frameworks like the "graph of thoughts". We are firmly in the "Age of Computation", where breakthroughs in AI are synonymous with the ability to harness and optimize massive computational resources. However, this rapid growth in computational demands comes with a critical challenge: energy limitations. Around the globe, new power plants are being constructed to meet the demands of AI workloads, underscoring the urgent need for efficiency to ensure these advancements benefit humanity sustainably. Especially in Singapore, such resources may be scarce and hinder the ability of the country’s researchers to advance in this most important field. Our collaborative efforts with the A*STAR Institute of High Performance Computing (IHPC) and other partners in Singapore, such as NTU, could be pivotal in this field, driving the development and implementation of innovative AI methods and saving millions of dollars in compute time while accelerating scientific productivity . To enhance the efficacy of AI for Science models, it is imperative to integrate simulations that encode prior scientific knowledge within these AI frameworks . This integration is aimed at creating new models imbued with robust prior knowledge, such as simulated behaviours defined by fundamental equations and conservation laws. Our approach involves the close collaboration of experts from A*STAR / IHPC, who bring extensive experience in high-performance computing and AI-driven scientific research. Together, we aim to push the boundaries of what AI can achieve in scientific domains, ensuring that simulations and AI methodologies are combined to produce highly accurate and reliable models. Job description The Postdoctoral Researcher will be co-leading the development of a novel open-source accelerator communication library (OCCL). This communication library should support point-to-point as well as collective communication calls. It should allow communication initiated by the host, as well as communication initiated within accelerator device kernels. It should support a wide range of devices and network substrates, such as NVLINK and next-generation ethernet networks. Some key components in the work are:
• Co-lead the design and development of an open-source accelerator communication library (OCCL) supporting point-to-point and collective communication for distributed AI workloads.
• Design and implement communication primitives and algorithms optimised for machine learning training and inference w

As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions. Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) . The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems. Project background The current era of artificial intelligence is predominantly driven by advances in computational power and infrastructure. As models scale to unprecedented sizes, their capabilities are enhanced through strategies such as reinforcement learning (RL) and innovative frameworks like the "graph of thoughts". We are firmly in the "Age of Computation", where breakthroughs in AI are synonymous with the ability to harness and optimize massive computational resources. However, this rapid growth in computational demands comes with a critical challenge: energy limitations. Around the globe, new power plants are being constructed to meet the demands of AI workloads, underscoring the urgent need for efficiency to ensure these advancements benefit humanity sustainably. Especially in Singapore, such resources may be scarce and hinder the ability of the country’s researchers to advance in this most important field. Our collaborative efforts with the A*STAR Institute of High Performance Computing (IHPC) and other partners in Singapore, such as NTU, could be pivotal in this field, driving the development and implementation of innovative AI methods and saving millions of dollars in compute time while accelerating scientific productivity . To enhance the efficacy of AI for Science models, it is imperative to integrate simulations that encode prior scientific knowledge within these AI frameworks . This integration is aimed at creating new models imbued with robust prior knowledge, such as simulated behaviours defined by fundamental equations and conservation laws. Our approach involves the close collaboration of experts from A*STAR / IHPC, who bring extensive experience in high-performance computing and AI-driven scientific research. Together, we aim to push the boundaries of what AI can achieve in scientific domains, ensuring that simulations and AI methodologies are combined to produce highly accurate and reliable models. Job description The Postdoctoral Researcher will be co-leading the development of a novel open-source accelerator communication library (OCCL). This communication library should support point-to-point as well as collective communication calls. It should allow communication initiated by the host, as well as communication initiated within accelerator device kernels. It should support a wide range of devices and network substrates, such as NVLINK and next-generation ethernet networks. Some key components in the work are:
• Co-lead the design and development of an open-source accelerator communication library (OCCL) supporting point-to-point and collective communication for distributed AI workloads.
• Design and implement communication primitives and algorithms optimised for machine learning training and inference w

descriptionByLocale.it:
PhD Researcher - AI TokCart 100%, Singapore, fixed-term Drucken The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF) , as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions. Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) . The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems. Project background The healthcare systems of the future must harness data effectively to support clinicians, allowing them to focus on patient care while leveraging AIto detect patterns beyond human perception, enhance diagnostic accuracy, optimise workflows, improve risk assessment and communication. Developing AI models that address these needs is particularly urgent in ageing societies, where rising patient numbers coincide with increasing workforce constraints. A major contributor to disability in older adults is impaired musculoskeletal (MSK) health, with fall-related fractures representing a central research focus for our group. Despite their substantial socioeconomic burden, progress in prevention and screening has been limited, partly because fall and fracture risks are often addressed independently, despite their shared underlying mechanisms. A promising direction for AI in healthcare is the seamless integration of clinical image-based foundation models that can be fine-tuned across multiple use cases. In this project, we aim to develop cross-modal AI models for MSK health evaluation by linking diverse clinical imaging datasets. The central innovation is the creation of a shared, tokenized latent space that enables data translation, risk modelling, and local deployment, even in settings with limited imaging data. Particular emphasis will be placed on integrating advanced biomechanical markers of bone health into AI workflows, supporting more precise and clinically actionable risk assessment. Job description The PhD candidate will be embedded into a team of researchers that is working on developing large medical image-based AI models for managing MSK health. Some key components in the work are:
• Pretraining, adapting, and evaluating foundation models for medical image data using self-supervised and multimodal representation learning.
• Developing cross-modal image modelling methods, including cross-modal translation, multimodal fusion, and related generative or representation-learning approaches.
• Evaluating the learned models on clinically relevant downstream tasks, such as bone health assessment, anatomical and biomechanical biomarker estimation, and fracture-risk-related prediction.
• Co-supervision of MSc and BSc students. Please note that the employment will be at the Singapore-ETH Centre in Singapore, and local working regulations will apply. Funding is provided for up to four years. After successful completion of studies, the PhD degree will be awarded by ETH Zurich. Profile
• Applicants should hold an MSc degree and have a strong background in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related quantitative discipline.
• Candidates should be capable of working largely independently on complex rese

Student Research Assistant in Environmental Economics 10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken As part of an SNSF-funded Ambizione project , Dr Sarah Meier studies the economic dimensions of forest loss and environmental change, with a focus on biodiversity, human well-being, and policy design. The project examines how interconnected natural and economic systems shape outcomes related to land use, conservation, and climate-related risks. We are seeking a Research Assistant for 6 months , with the option to extension. The position is available immediately or by agreement. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The role supports ongoing research activities within the project, including engagement with academic literature, empirical analysis, and data work. This position requires the ability to engage rigorously with academic research. Responsibilities include critically assessing published work, understanding empirical and theoretical approaches, and contributing to the synthesis of research insights. The role is suited to candidates with a strong interest in environmental economics, excellent analytical skills, and the capacity for independent, critical thinking. Project background Environmental change is increasingly shaped by interconnected systems linking land use, biodiversity, climate, and human well-being. Forest loss, driven by both human activity and climate-related hazards, has wide-ranging economic, ecological, and social consequences. While a substantial body of research examines these processes, insights remain fragmented across disciplines and often fail to capture broader system-wide interactions. This project investigates the economic dimensions of forest loss and its implications for biodiversity, human health, and policy design. It aims to develop a structured understanding of these interconnected processes by integrating insights from existing research with empirical analysis. Particular emphasis is placed on identifying gaps in the literature, analysing underlying economic mechanisms, and generating policy-relevant evidence using causal inference methods and spatial data. Waldverlust, der sowohl durch menschliche Aktivitäten als auch durch klimabedingte Gefahren verursacht wird, hat weitreichende wirtschaftliche, ökologische und soziale Folgen. descriptionByLocale.it:
Ricercatore post-dottorato in AI per l'inferenza delle informazioni sul clima

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Il ricercatore post-dottorato avanzerà l'applicazione di AI, grandi modelli di lingua (LLM), e l'apprendimento automatico per estrarre le informazioni climatiche affidabili dai dataset di sistema geospaziale e terrestre su larga scala, all'interno del programma NCCR CLIM+. Il ruolo collega la scienza del clima e l'intelligenza artificiale, sviluppando nuovi metodi per l'analisi dei dati climatici, il downscaling e la sintesi utilizzando modelli di fondazione (ad esempio Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) su una piattaforma HPC all'avanguardia. Il ricercatore condurrà una ricerca scientifica pubblica mentre costruirà strumenti e condotte che servono la più ampia comunità CLIM+. La posizione è supervisionata congiuntamente dal Prof. Andreas Prein, dal Prof. Erich Fischer e dal Prof. Reto Knutti all'ETH di Zurigo e dal Prof. Markus Leippold all'Università di Zurigo.

Sfondo del progetto

La scienza del clima sta generando volumi in rapida crescita di dati satellitari, di rianalisi e di modelli, creando nuove opportunità ma anche grandi sfide per trasformare i dati in informazioni robuste e utili. Questo progetto svilupperà metodi basati su AI per estrarre, sintetizzare e interpretare le informazioni climatiche affidabili dai dataset del sistema terrestre di grandi e complessi all'interno del programma NCCR CLIM+.

Descrizione del lavoro

• Progettare, sviluppare e applicare metodi AI/ML — compresi i modelli di lingua di grandi dimensioni (LLM) e i modelli di fondazione (Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) — per estrarre, sintetizzare e ragionare su informazioni climatiche affidabili da geospaziali su larga scala, satelliti, rianalisi e dataset del modello climatico

• Apprendimento avanzato della macchina fisica-consapevole per la rappresentazione del processo climatico su scala di chilometri

• Implementazione e valutazione di modelli AI generativi avanzati per la riduzione del clima ad alta risoluzione, l'assimilazione dei dati, l'emulazione e il post-elaborazione di previsioni meteo-clima

• Sviluppare metodi di quantificazione dell'incertezza nelle proiezioni in calo dei rischi climatici estremi e climatici

• Lavorare con i dati del sistema terrestre multimodale tra cui uscite di modelli climatici satelliti, aerei, in-situ, rianalisi e ad alta risoluzione

• Costruire strumenti software robusti e scalabili e datadotti per il trattamento di grandi dataset geospaziali, consentendo ai partner di progetto CLIM+ e alla più ampia comunità di ricerca di sfruttare le informazioni climatiche basate su AI

• Sviluppare e mantenere flussi di lavoro di ricerca riproducibili utilizzando moderne pratiche di ingegneria del software (controllo di conversione, test, documentazione, containerizzazione)

• Condurre ricerca scientifica originale e pubblica che genera nuove intuizioni all'incrocio di AI e scienza del clima

• Scrivere e presentare giornali peer-reviewed, presenti a conferenze internazionali, e contribuire a NCCR CLIM+ reporting e sovvenzioni proposte

• Assicurarsi che la ricerca produce sia conoscenze scientifiche che contributi metodologici sul campo

• Collaborare a stretto contatto con i gruppi di ricerca di ETH (Prein, Knutti, Fischer) e UZH (Leippold, Vaghefi, Colesanti Senni) per allineare lo sviluppo di AI con le domande di ricerca sulla scienza del clima

• Partecipare a attività di programma CLIM+, workshop e iniziative cross-project

• Contribuire alla supervisione di studenti e tirocinanti, se del caso

Profilo

• PhD in scienze del clima, scienza atmosferica, informatica, scienza dei dati, fisica, matematica applicata, telerilevamento o un campo correlato

• Forte record di pubblicazione in AI, machine learning, o Earth system science

• Esperienza con grandi set di dati geospaziali, telerilevamento, rianalisi o uscita del modello clima/tizzato

• Proficienza in Python e strutture di apprendimento automatico come PyTorch, TensorFlow, o JAX

• Esperienza con HPC e GPU

• Familiarità con i modelli di fondazione / LLM; interesse nei flussi di lavoro riproducibili

• Interesse a flussi di lavoro riproducibili e sviluppo di software scientifico

• Stile di lavoro indipendente, proattivo e collaborativo con forti capacità di comunicazione

descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Researcher in AI for Climate Information Inference

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The postdoctoral researcher will advance the application of AI, large language models (LLMs), and machine learning to extract trustworthy climate information from large-scale geospatial and Earth system datasets, within the NCCR CLIM+ program. The role bridges climate science and AI, developing novel methods for climate data analysis, downscaling, and synthesis using foundation models (e.g., Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) on a cutting-edge HPC platform. The researcher will conduct publishable scientific research while building tools and pipelines that serve the broader CLIM+ community. The position is jointly supervised by Prof. Andreas Prein, Prof. Erich Fischer, and Prof. Reto Knutti at ETH Zurich and Prof. Markus Leippold at the University of Zurich.

Project background

Climate science is generating rapidly growing volumes of satellite, reanalysis, and model data, creating new opportunities but also major challenges for turning data into robust and useful information. This project will develop AI-based methods to extract, synthesize, and interpret trustworthy climate information from large and complex Earth system datasets within the NCCR CLIM+ programme.

Job description

• Design, develop, and apply AI/ML methods — including large language models (LLMs) and foundation models (Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) — to extract, synthesize, and reason about trustworthy climate information from large-scale geospatial, satellite, reanalysis, and climate model datasets

• Advanced physics-aware machine learning for kilometer-scale climate process representation

• Implement and evaluate advanced generative AI models for high-resolution climate downscaling, data assimilation, emulation, and post-processing of weather-to-climate predictions

• Develop methods for uncertainty quantification in downscaled projections of extreme weather and climate hazards

• Work with multimodal Earth system data including satellite, airborne, in-situ, reanalysis, and high-resolution climate model outputs

• Build robust, scalable software tools and data pipelines for processing large geospatial datasets, enabling CLIM+ project partners and the broader research community to leverage AI-driven climate information

• Develop and maintain reproducible research workflows using modern software engineering practices (version control, testing, documentation, containerization)

• Conduct original, publishable scientific research generating novel insights at the intersection of AI and climate science

• Write and submit peer-reviewed journal papers, present at international conferences, and contribute to NCCR CLIM+ reporting and grant proposals

• Ensure that the research produces both scientific insight and methodological contributions to the field

• Collaborate closely with research groups at ETH (Prein, Knutti, Fischer) and UZH (Leippold, Vaghefi, Colesanti Senni) to align AI development with climate science research questions

• Participate in CLIM+ programme activities, workshops, and cross-project initiatives

• Contribute to supervision of students and interns where appropriate

Profile

• PhD in climate science, atmospheric science, computer science, data science, physics, applied mathematics, remote sensing, or a related field

• Strong publication record in AI, machine learning, or Earth system data science

• Experience with large geospatial datasets, remote sensing, reanalyses, or climate/weather model output

• Proficiency in Python and machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX

• Experience with HPC and GPU-accelerated computing

• Familiarity with foundation models / LLMs; interest in reproducible workflows

• Interest in reproducible workflows and scientific software development

• Independent, proactive, and collaborative working style with strong communication skills

Die Rolle überbrückt die Klimawissenschaft und KI, die Entwicklung neuartiger Methoden für die Klimadatenanalyse, Downscaling und Synthese mit Basismodellen (z.B. Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) auf einer hochmodernen HPC-Plattform. Der Forscher wird wissenschaftliche Forschung veröffentlichen, während er Werkzeuge und Pipelines baut, die der breiteren CLIM+ Gemeinschaft dienen. Die Position wird gemeinsam von Prof. Andreas Prein, Prof. Erich Fischer, und Prof. Reto Knutti an der ETH Zürich und Prof. Markus Leippold an der Universität Zürich betreut.

Projekt Hintergrund

Die Klimawissenschaft generiert schnell wachsende Mengen an Satelliten-, Reanalyse- und Modelldaten und schafft neue Möglichkeiten, aber auch große Herausforderungen, Daten in robuste und nützliche Informationen zu verwandeln. Dieses Projekt wird AI-basierte Methoden entwickeln, um vertrauenswürdige Klimainformationen aus großen und komplexen Erdsystemdatensätzen im NCCR CLIM+-Programm zu extrahieren, zu synthetisieren und zu interpretieren.

Jobbeschreibung

• Entwicklung, Entwicklung und Anwendung von KI/ML-Methoden – einschließlich großer Sprachmodelle (LLMs) und Grundmodellen (Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) – zur Extraktion, Synthese und Vernunft von vertrauenswürdigen Klimainformationen aus großflächigen Geospatial-, Satelliten-, Reanalyse- und Klimamodelldatensätzen

• Entwicklung von Methoden zur Ungewissheitsquantifizierung in skalierten Projektionen extremer Wetter- und Klimarisiken

• Bauen Sie robuste, skalierbare Software-Tools und Datenpipelines für die Verarbeitung großer geospatialer Datensätze, die es CLIM+ Projektpartnern und der breiteren Forschungsgemeinschaft ermöglichen, AI-gesteuerte Klimainformationen zu nutzen

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Chercheur postdoctoral en AI pour l'Inférence sur l'information climatique

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

imprimer
Drucken

Le chercheur postdoctoral fera progresser l'application de l'IA, des grands modèles linguistiques (LLM) et de l'apprentissage automatique afin d'extraire des informations fiables sur le climat à partir des ensembles de données géospatiales et des systèmes terrestres à grande échelle, dans le cadre du programme CLIM+ du CCNR. Le rôle est de relier la science du climat et l'IA, de développer de nouvelles méthodes d'analyse des données climatiques, de réduction de l'échelle et de synthèse à l'aide de modèles de base (p. ex. Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch) sur une plate-forme HPC de pointe. Le chercheur effectuera des recherches scientifiques publiables tout en construisant des outils et des pipelines au service de la communauté CLIM+. Ce poste est supervisé conjointement par le Prof. Andreas Prein, le Prof. Erich Fischer et le Prof. Reto Knutti à l'ETH Zurich et le Prof. Markus Leippold à l'Université de Zurich.

Contexte du projet

La science du climat génère des volumes en croissance rapide de données satellitaires, de réanalyses et de modèles, créant de nouvelles possibilités mais aussi des défis majeurs pour transformer les données en informations solides et utiles. Ce projet mettra au point des méthodes basées sur l'IA pour extraire, synthétiser et interpréter des informations fiables sur le climat à partir d'ensembles de données de grands systèmes terrestres complexes dans le cadre du programme CLIM+ du CCNR.

Description du poste

• Concevoir, mettre au point et appliquer des méthodes d'IA/ML, y compris des modèles en langage large (LLM) et des modèles de fondation (Google Earth AI, AlphaEarth, TerraTorch), afin d'extraire, de synthétiser et de raisonner des informations fiables sur le climat à partir de séries de données géospatiales, satellitaires, de réanalyse et de modèles climatiques à grande échelle

• Apprentissage avancé en physique pour la représentation des processus climatiques à l'échelle du kilomètre

• Mettre en œuvre et évaluer des modèles d'IA génériques avancés pour la réduction du climat à haute résolution, l'assimilation des données, l'émulation et le post-traitement des prévisions météorologiques au climat

• Mettre au point des méthodes de quantification de l'incertitude dans les projections à échelle réduite des risques météorologiques et climatiques extrêmes

• Travailler avec les données du système terrestre multimodal, y compris les résultats des modèles climatiques à haute résolution, aériens, in situ et réanalyse;

• Mettre au point des logiciels et des pipelines de données robustes et évolutifs pour le traitement de grands ensembles de données géospatiales, ce qui permettra aux partenaires du projet CLIM+ et à l'ensemble de la communauté de la recherche de tirer parti des informations climatiques issues de l'IA

• Développer et maintenir des flux de travail de recherche reproductibles à l'aide de pratiques modernes de génie logiciel (contrôle des versions, essais, documentation, conteneurisation)

• Mener une recherche scientifique originale, publiable, générant de nouvelles idées à l'intersection de l'IA et des sciences du climat

• Rédiger et soumettre des articles de revues examinés par les pairs, présents lors de conférences internationales, et contribuer aux propositions de rapports et de subventions du CCNR CLIM+

• Veiller à ce que la recherche produise des connaissances scientifiques et des contributions méthodologiques sur le terrain

• Collaborer étroitement avec les groupes de recherche de l'ETH (Prein, Knutti, Fischer) et de l'UZH (Leippold, Vaghefi, Colesanti Senni) pour aligner le développement de l'IA sur les questions de recherche en sciences du climat

• Participer aux activités, ateliers et initiatives intersectorielles du programme CLIM+

• Contribuer à la supervision des étudiants et des stagiaires, le cas échéant

Profil

• Doctorat en sciences du climat, en sciences atmosphériques, en informatique, en sciences des données, en physique, en mathématiques appliquées, en télédétection ou dans un domaine connexe

• Forte publication dans l'IA, l'apprentissage automatique ou la science des données du système terrestre

• Expérience des grands ensembles de données géospatiales, de la télédétection, des réanalyses ou de la production de modèles climatiques et météorologiques

• Compétence en Python et en cadres d'apprentissage automatique tels que PyTorch, TensorFlow ou JAX

• Expérience de l'informatique accélérée HPC et GPU

• Familiarité avec les modèles de fondation / LLM; intérêt pour les workflows reproductibles

• Intérêt pour les flux de travail reproductibles et le développement de logiciels scientifiques

• Style de travail indépendant, proactif et collaboratif avec de solides compétences en communication

Il vostro impegno crea le migliori condizioni per l'eccellenza nell'insegnamento, nella ricerca, nel trasferimento di conoscenze e nella sostenibilità dell'ETH Zurigo. In un'atmosfera aperta e stimolante, fiducia, affidabilità e rispetto reciproco costituiscono la base della nostra cooperazione. Vi offriamo non solo la sicurezza, ma anche una vasta gamma di possibilità per un ulteriore sviluppo. Ci aspettiamo che lavori in modo significativo
